Article Title: CBSE third-language rule: Supreme Court extends relaxations to Class VI students
Article Text:
SC extends Class VII-VIII relaxations to Class VI (PTI photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday directed the CBSE to extend to Class VI students the same exemptions and relaxations available to students of Classes VII and VIII under its newly introduced three-language scheme.Under the order, Class VI students will have to study the newly mandated third language, but they will not have to appear for a CBSE Board examination in that language when they reach Class X. The exemption is currently available to students who are in Classes VII and VIII.The Supreme Court has also extended another relaxation to Class VI students. Those already studying two non-native languages will be allowed to continue with the same combination and take one additional Bharatiya Bhasha as their third language.This means such students will not have to drop or change either of their existing languages to accommodate the two regional languages required under the new language scheme.The directions bring Class VI students on par with the current Classes VII and VIII batches in terms of the exemptions and flexibility available under the CBSE's three-language policy.
Article Summary: Supreme Court orders CBSE to extend same exemptions and relaxations to Class VI students. Students will have to study the newly mandated third language, but will not have to appear for a CBSE Board examination in that language. The exemption is currently available to students who are in Classes VII and VIII.

Article Title: Stock market crash today: BSE Sensex crashes over 1,100 points, investors lose Rs 8.92 lakh crore - top reasons for fall
Article Text:
Both indices crashed over 1% amid the intensifying Iran-US conflict.

Why is stock market crashing today?

Iran-US conflict escalates

Oil prices jump

Bond yields soar

Rupee tumbles

FII outflows

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

Stock market crash today: BSE Sensex and Nifty50 , the Indian equity benchmarks tanked in morning trade on Monday as persistently high crude oil prices and a spike in US bond yields added to investors’ woes. Both indices crashed over 1% amid the intensifying Iran-US conflict.While Sensex crashed over 1,100 points, Nifty50 went below 22,800. BSE Sensex ended the day at 72,771.72, down 1,124 points or 1.52%. Nifty50 closed at 22,780.25, down 360 points or 1.56%.The selloff also erased nearly Rs 8.92 lakh crore from the combined market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies, taking it down to around Rs 474 lakh crore.Also Read | Two years ago Sensex hit lifetime high: What went wrong after that & what’s the road ahead? Every one of the 30 Sensex stocks was trading in negative territory. Bajaj Finance, Kotak Mahindra Bank and HDFC Bank led the decline. The weakness was not restricted to large-cap stocks. The Nifty Smallcap 100 and Nifty Midcap 100 indices also declined by more than 1% each.Indian equities were also tracking the broader weakness across several Asian markets, where stocks came under pressure amid the surge in oil prices.South Korea’s Kospi declined more than 2%, while China’s Shanghai Composite dropped over 1.7%. Japan’s Nikkei, however, posted muted gains.Tensions between Iran and the US intensified after US President Donald Trump rejected Iran's proposal for a seven-day ceasefire along with the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.Speaking to reporters on Saturday, Trump said, "I reject this agreement. They want an agreement to be made under which the Strait of Hormuz is immediately opened, because they are severely failing.”Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, meanwhile, said the country would remain firm and would not back down in the face of the US and Israel.The latest developments in the Middle East triggered another sharp rise in crude prices, with oil gaining 2% and moving close to $107 per barrel as markets factored in the possibility of further disruption to shipments. JPMorgan said it could no longer clearly assess where oil prices were headed and, for the first time since the Iran war began in February, said it did not have a defined baseline scenario for the market.US bond yields continued their climb, reaching fresh multi-year highs and adding another layer of pressure on equities. The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note moved further above 5.2%, its highest level since 2004. The 30-year US bond yield also crossed 5.5%, while the yield on two-year Treasury notes, which generally moves alongside expectations of Federal Reserve rate hikes, rose above 4.9%.Higher bond yields generally increase the attractiveness of debt markets for investors, which can put additional pressure on riskier assets such as equities.The Indian rupee weakened by 14 paise to 95.89 against the US dollar in early trading. Forex traders are increasingly concerned about the currency breaching the psychologically important 96 level against the dollar, with the rupee facing pressure from elevated oil prices, higher US Treasury yields and a stronger dollar.“Volatility in crude and gold, along with a rise in the dollar, limited the rupee’s ability to sustain gains. Going ahead, currency movement is likely to remain range-bound amid global commodity and dollar volatility. Rupee range can be seen between 95.50-96.50,” said Jateen Trivedi, VP Research Analyst - Commodity and Currency, LKP Securities.Foreign investors continued to sell Indian equities on Friday, offloading shares worth a net Rs 3,694 crore, according to provisional NSE data.VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments, said the shift in FPI flows towards the negative side after positive inflows in July and August had become visible earlier this month. He said the selling trend has continued, with total equity outflows through exchanges reaching Rs 25,682 crore so far this month.
Article Summary: BSE Sensex and Nifty50 crashed over 1% amid the intensifying Iran-US conflict. Bajaj Finance, Kotak Mahindra Bank and HDFC Bank led the decline. The selloff also erased nearly Rs 8.92 lakh crore from the combined market capitalisation.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Spot silver fell 2.6% to $62.64 per ounce, platinum declined 2.1% to $1,741.45 and palladium dropped 2.1% to $1,239.95.Gold remains under pressure as both bond yields and crude oil prices moved higher. The increase in oil prices, driven by mixed indications on supply flows, kept inflation risks firmly in focus among investors.Iran said diplomacy remained the only route to resolving its conflict with the United States and Israel. This came after US President Donald Trump said he had rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and bring the fighting to an end.Oil prices later recovered more than 1%.According to experts, the primary reason for prices falling sharply is the rise in US bond yields.Ashish Rajodiya, Head – Commodities, PL Capital says, “MCX Gold (December contract) is trading at Rs 1,50,500 per 10 grams, down Rs 2,700 or 1.80% today, extending its slide for a second straight week. Uncertainty around the US-Iran conflict continues to keep risk sentiment volatile. Recent diplomatic efforts have produced mixed signals, with Iran indicating readiness for both negotiations and renewed conflict, while the US has rejected Iran’s latest proposal, although further talks through mediators remain possible. ”“Gold is trading at $4185, down more than 2.%, and it is facing sharp selling pressure as geopolitical uncertainty, a firm Dollar and higher bond yields with 5.22% on 10yrs weigh on bullion as higher probability of rate hike prices in. The lack of clarity over a potential US-Iran settlement is keeping safe-haven demand volatile,” he adds.Ashish Rajodiya is of the view that gold prices have support at Rs 1,48,000 and Rs 1,46,000, with resistance at Rs 1,52,500 and Rs 1,55,000.“The metal's next move likely hinges on two threads converging at once: the Fed's October rate decision, and whether the recent signs of renewed US-Iran diplomatic engagement on Hormuz firm up into an actual de-escalation,” he says.“A dovish surprise from the Fed or confirmed progress on Iran talks could spark a sharp bounce toward resistance, while continued hawkish signals or a stalled Iran negotiation would likely extend the slide toward the lower support band,” he adds.Manoj Kumar Jain of Prithvi Finmart expects gold and silver to see continued volatility this week as traders track movements in crude oil prices and the dollar index, along with geopolitical tensions and developments in the US-Iran peace talks.For gold, he sees support at $4,284-4,260 per troy ounce, with resistance placed at $4,355-4,388. For silver, his support levels are Rs 2,33,000-2,30,400, with resistance at Rs 2,36,600-2,38,800.Jain told ET that investors should wait for further developments in the US-Iran peace talks before initiating fresh positions in gold and silver. For those already holding long positions, he recommended keeping a strict stop-loss below Rs 1,49,600 for gold and below Rs 2,30,000 for silver, based on daily closing levels.

Article Title: Brij Bhushan acquittal challenged over ‘stereotypical assumptions’ about sexual assault victims
Article Text:
Wrestlers challenge acquittal, cite ‘stereotypical assumptions’

NEW DELHI: The Rouse Avenue court has issued notice to former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and others on an appeal challenging his acquittal in a sexual harassment case involving women wrestlers.Special Judge Dig Vinay Singh sought a response to the appeal and listed the matter for hearing on October 9. The court also directed that the original affidavit and orders containing the names of the victims be placed in a sealed envelope. It further directed the appellant to file a copy of the petition with the victims’ names redacted.The appeal challenges the August 3 order of the Rouse Avenue court, Brij Bhushan and Vinod Tomar in the case. The wrestlers have contended that the acquittal order is unsustainable in law and is based on a “manifestly erroneous and selective appreciation of the evidence on record”.The appeal has contended that the impugned order proceeds on conjectures and surmises, fails to apply binding and well-settled principles of law, and, in material part, rests its reasoning on “archaic and stereotypical assumptions” about the “expected” behaviour of victims of sexual assault and harassment, rather than on a fair, evidence-based assessment after taking into account the circumstances of the victims.The case stems from an FIR filed by Delhi Police following a complaint by a woman wrestler during Singh’s tenure as WFI chief. The police had invoked Sections 354, 354-D, 354-A, 506(1) and 109 of the Indian Penal Code.Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Ashwani Panwar had acquitted Singh and Tomar after a trial that was conducted in a closed courtroom. The two were tried in connection with allegations of sexual harassment of women wrestlers in India and abroad.Delhi Police had filed a 1,500-page charge sheet against Singh and Tomar on June 15, 2023, following its investigation into the allegations.The women wrestlers had earlier staged a protest at Jantar Mantar, following which the FIR was registered by Delhi Police based on the complaint.Advocate Rajiv Mohan, assisted by Rehan Khan and Rishabh Bhati, represented Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, while senior advocate Rebecca John appeared for the victims and complainants.
Article Summary: The appeal challenges the August 3 order of the Rouse Avenue court, Brij Bhushan and Vinod Tomar in the case. The wrestlers have contended that the acquittal order is unsustainable in law and is based on a “manifestly erroneous and selective appreciation of the evidence on record”

Article Title: CCPA penalises Amazon, Flipkart, JioMart for selling unregistered herbicide
Article Text:
Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed penalties of Rs 10 lakh

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed penalties of Rs 10 lakh each on Amazon and Flipkart, and Rs 5 lakh on JioMart, for selling and advertising an unregistered agrochemical product, Cyclosinone Herbicide.Cyclosinone Herbicide is marketed as a granular weed-control product used to prevent and eliminate broadleaf and grassy weeds in lawns, gardens and agricultural fields.In separate orders issued recently, the consumer watchdog directed the e-commerce marketplaces to immediately discontinue the false and misleading advertisements and conduct a self-audit of their platforms to identify and remove products that violate the law or pose a risk to consumers’ life and safety.The CCPA initiated proceedings after the department of agriculture and farmers’ welfare forwarded a complaint it had received from the Crop Care Federation of India (CCFI) regarding the sale and advertisement of the unregistered herbicide through e-commerce and digital media platforms.During the investigation, the agriculture department informed CCPA that the import, manufacture, sale, transport, distribution and use of insecticides and pesticides are regulated under the Insecticides Act, 1968, and the Insecticides Rules to safeguard human beings and animals from potential risks.The department told the authority that no chemical named Cyclosinone is included in the Schedule to the Insecticides Act. However, a product marketed as “Cyclosinone Herbicide” was being sold through online platforms without disclosing the chemical name of its active ingredient or its composition.“It is currently being marketed illegally because it bypasses the mandatory safety, bio-efficacy, quality and legal checks required under the Insecticides Act,” the department said in its submission to CCPA.The authority rejected the e-commerce companies’ argument that they could not be held responsible for products listed by third-party sellers. The CCPA said online marketplaces cannot disown their statutory obligation to protect consumers and are required to exercise due diligence to prevent the sale of products that are illegal or hazardous.
Article Summary: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed penalties of Rs 10 lakh each on Amazon and Flipkart, and Rs 5 lakh on JioMart. Cyclosinone Herbicide is marketed as a granular weed-control product used to prevent and eliminate broadleaf and grassy weeds.

Article Title: Boeing flags 737 MAX glitch that may turn off auto pilot
Article Text:
A software issue could disengage the B737 MAX autopilot during certain go-arounds when pilots alter the aircraft’s planned altitude or flight path.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Boeing has identified a software issue that could potentially lead to auto pilot disengaging during certain go-arounds (aborting landing to take off again and make a second attempt) on the B737 MAX when pilots change their planned altitude and path. India has about 100 of these aircraft between Air India Express and Akasa.Aviation insiders say this is not a safety scare and Boeing has issued an advisory to pilots regarding what to do in the rare event of a B737 MAX going around and then the altitude window being changed from what is in the system for that particular sector.A Boeing spokesperson said: "Last month, we informed all 737 operators about a software issue where pilots may not have access to automated flight guidance during a specific landing scenario. We shared information with operators that reinforced existing pilot procedures for safely handling such cases. Our engineers are working on a software update to permanently address the issue."A spokesperson for Akasa said: "We are closely coordinating with Boeing and can confirm there is no impact to safety... Our aircraft continue to operate safely in accordance with established procedures and applicable regulatory requirements."AI Express has over 50 of these planes.US Federal Aviation Admi-nistration has said in a statem-ent that it will "convene a corrective action review board and take immediate action if it identifies a safety concern".What was to be Boeing's answer to rival Airbus's best-selling A320 new engine option which boasts lower fuel burns, the B737 MAX came under intense scrutiny soon after it entered commercial passenger service in May 2017. Two back-to-back MAX crashes within five months - Lion Air in Oct 2018 and Ethiopian Airlines in March 2019 - that left 346 people dead led to the aircraft being grounded globally in March 2019. After Boeing made some crucial changes, the aircraft was allowed to fly again in Dec 2020.
Article Summary: A software issue could disengage the B737 MAX autopilot during certain go- arounds when pilots alter the aircraft’s planned altitude or flight path. India has about 100 of these aircraft between Air India Express and Akasa. Boeing has issued an advisory to pilots regarding what to do in the rare event.

Article Title: When ‘secret spot’ goes viral: The tourism trap of too many views, too many visitors
Article Text:
Digital demand can surge faster than physical infrastructure can adapt.

From travel guide to visual trigger

A viral viewpoint

The algorithm loves the photogenic

Can an algorithm create overtourism?

The reel doesn't show the queue

When the road becomes the bottleneck

Too Viral to Handle

The environmental bill arrives later

Water is part of the tourism footprint too

The cost nobody sees on the reel

The local economy has something to gain—and lose

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

From viral tourism to responsible discovery

Tourism brings people, places, and cultures closer. It creates opportunities for communities, supports livelihoods, and contributes significantly to economic development. Globally, travel and tourism contributed $10.9 trillion, or 10% of global GDP, in 2024, supporting 357 million jobs and generating $1.9 trillion in international visitor spending.But the way people decide where to go is changing - and increasingly, the journey begins before the journey, inside a phone.On World Tourism Day 2026, observed on September 27, the global tourism sector is discussing how digital technology and Artificial Intelligence can redesign tourism. India arrives at that conversation amid extraordinary growth: Domestic Tourist Visits reached 428.55 crore in 2025, up from 67.7 crore in 2021, while Foreign Tourist Visits rose from 0.1 crore to 2.53 crore. Foreign Exchange Earnings from tourism increased from Rs 63,978 crore to Rs 2,76,831 crore over the same period, according to the Ministry of Tourism.The opportunity is enormous. So, is the question increasingly confronting destinations: what happens when a beautiful place becomes more famous online than it is capable of being on the ground?That is the emerging Instagram destination problem.Instagram Reels have fundamentally changed travel discovery. A 20-second video can compress a mountain road, turquoise lake, café, waterfall or village into an irresistible sequence of drone shots, music, transitions and carefully selected frames.The Government of India has itself recognised social media's growing role in tourism. A Ministry of Tourism study titled “Social Media as an Influencer among Foreign Tourists Visiting India”, conducted through the Indian Institute of Tourism and Travel Management, examined social media's influence on foreign visitors.The ministry subsequently acknowledged the importance of Instagram, YouTube, influencers, vloggers and user-generated content in tourism promotion. Tourism policy expert Hemant Joshi, CEO of Atithi Foundation, says the challenge is that visitor demand can grow far faster than a destination’s infrastructure, carrying capacity and local ecosystem can handle. “We are increasingly seeing this in fragile mountain and rural destinations, where a viral post can almost instantly translate into traffic, waste, pressure on water and other local infrastructure, and disruption for communities. Recent experiences in places such as Manali, Ladakh and the Nilgiris are a reminder of this gap,” he said.Once someone interacts with travel content, similar destinations can flood their feed. Discovery therefore becomes less deliberate. A person who has never heard of a particular valley, café or viewpoint can encounter it repeatedly until an unfamiliar place starts feeling like a destination they need to experience.The problem is not that social media makes people travel. Travel inspiration has always existed.The difference is scale, speed and concentration. Algorithms reward content that attracts attention. Visually dramatic places are naturally suited to short-form video. That creates a feedback loop:beautiful destination → engaging Reel → high views → more creators → more travellers → more content → even more visibility.Travel enthusiast and hotel manager working in Gurgaon, Nitish Srivastava, who also creates travel content, says algorithms have a soft spot for what already grabs eyeballs. “So creators can end up repeatedly visiting the same popular places because they know the audience will respond,” he added.He said a creator can show the experience of a fragile place without necessarily turning its precise location into a mass-tourism instruction manual. “You can still share the experience without turning it into a ‘go here before everyone finds out’ trend. For me, protecting a place is more important than getting a few extra views,” Nitish said.Delhi-based traveller Harsh Shivam, who likes sharing travel-related content on social media, similarly argues that creators should exercise judgement when revealing particularly fragile or previously uncrowded locations. “Location is obviously an important part of travel content, but there is a difference between telling people roughly where a place is and giving them precise directions to a spot that may not be able to handle a sudden influx of visitors,” said Harsh.But he also highlights the other side: “Increased tourism can create opportunities for local businesses and communities.””That is the central paradox.Visibility can be economic development. The same visibility can become environmental pressure.There is another problem: social media shows a destination, but rarely shows its carrying capacity. A reel might capture the waterfall. It probably won't show the road leading to it clogged with vehicles.It might show a pristine mountain lake. It probably won't show the plastic waste left behind.It might show an empty viewpoint. It won't necessarily tell you that the shot was taken at 6 am, during a brief window between crowds. “A place may only look the way it does in a particular season, or the experience may change significantly depending on the time of year. That context can be important in setting realistic expectations for people planning a visit,” said Harsh.Srivastava says his own experience has repeatedly demonstrated this gap: “Social media usually shows the best few seconds—the perfect light, empty viewpoint and cinematic angle.”India's tourism numbers make this increasingly important.Official Uttarakhand statistics show how dramatically visitor numbers can concentrate at individual destinations. Kedarnath recorded 243,012 visitors in 2021, rising to 1,564,248 in 2022 and 1,958,863 in 2023. Badrinath rose from 199,409 in 2021 to 1,780,429 in 2023. Tehri recorded more than 3.76 million tourist visits in 2023, according to Uttarakhand Tourism.The issue isn't simply how many people enter a state. It is where they go, when they arrive and whether local infrastructure can absorb the concentration. Roads, parking, public toilets, accommodation, drinking water, sewage systems, emergency services and waste collection all have finite capacity. And when tourism growth is faster than infrastructure, the first visible sign may not be a tourism statistic. It may be a traffic jam.Government research shows that the environmental consequences are not theoretical.A Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change report submitted before the National Green Tribunal documented significant waste pressures associated with tourism in Uttarakhand. Research cited in the report, in January 2025 found that 71% of the total solid waste generated in the Valley of Flowers was produced in only 37 days. Estimated waste generation was approximately 364 grams per visitor per day on the Gomukh trek and 580 grams per visitor per day on the Kedarkantha trek.These numbers reveal an important characteristic of tourism pollution: seasonality and concentration matter.A place can cope with relatively modest visitor numbers for much of the year and still experience severe pressure during a short viral or peak-tourism window.Ladakh offers another stark example. A carrying-capacity study by the GB Pant National Institute of Himalayan Environment examined tourism pressure in the Leh Town Complex. The research recorded rapid growth in accommodation, air traffic and tourist influx, alongside concerns over waste generation and disposal. Ladakh's ecological vulnerability makes the equation particularly sensitive. Water, waste treatment, roads and energy are not infinitely expandable simply because Instagram demand rises.According to Kedarnath Nagar Panchayat data obtained through an RTI, Kedarnath generated 50.30 metric tonnes of waste between April and August 2026, more than 2.5 times the entire 2025 total.Tourism's environmental footprint is also much bigger than litter.Niti Aayog's work on sustainable tourism in the Indian Himalayan Region highlights pressures involving water consumption, groundwater extraction, energy, accommodation, transportation and solid waste. That is why “hidden gem” is not necessarily synonymous with “sustainable destination.”A small community may have a beautiful landscape but limited sewage treatment, parking, waste collection, medical facilities or water supply.Goa shows that even beaches have a limitThe carrying-capacity question is not confined to the Himalayas. Goa recorded 10.8 million tourist arrivals in 2025, according to the state's tourism department.An assessment placed before the National Green Tribunal found that, using a criterion of 10 square metres per visitor, carrying capacity was exceeded at beaches including Palolem, Agonda, Siridao, Vainguinim and Coco Beach.The problem is therefore not “Instagram versus tourism.” It is tourism growth versus destination capacity.It would be simplistic to portray viral tourism as entirely destructive. A formerly overlooked destination gaining attention can mean more customers for homestays, restaurants, taxis, guides, artisans and small retailers.But benefits are not automatically distributed equally.If visitor numbers rise faster than local capacity, residents can face congestion, waste, water stress, rising costs and disruption to everyday life. Meanwhile, businesses may become increasingly dependent on a tourism boom they did not necessarily create or control.India’s tourism challenge is therefore no longer simply about attracting visitors, but about distributing them intelligently. As Joshi puts it, “Digital platforms can be used to distribute demand by making credible, attractive alternatives discoverable rather than concentrating everyone on the same few locations.”Destinations, he argues, must plan for demand rather than chase it. “The objective should not be to make destinations less popular, but to make tourism growth more manageable, more geographically distributed and more valuable to the communities that host it.”
Article Summary: On World Tourism Day 2026, the global tourism sector is discussing how digital technology and Artificial Intelligence can redesign tourism. India arrives at that conversation amid extraordinary growth: Domestic Tourist Visits reached 428.55 crore in 2025. Globally, travel and tourism contributed $10.9 trillion, or 10% of global GDP, in 2024.

NEW DELHI: With EPFO increasing the mandatory wage ceiling from Rs 15,000 a month to Rs 25,000, employees will now contribute Rs 3,000 (at 12% contribution of Rs 25,000 wage) towards their PF savings from Rs 1,800 earlier, govt said in a set of FAQs released. But if an employee earns, say, Rs 35,000 a month, the mandatory PF contribution will be Rs 6,000 (Rs 3,000 from employee and employers each), with no amount going towards pension as EPS is available only to those whose wages do not exceed the EPFO wage ceiling.The retirement savings agency said the new regime kicked in from Sept 17 and asked employers to review contractor compliance, wherever contract labour is engaged, and update its payroll systems.Allaying employee fears of attempts to pass on the contribution by deducting more from salaries, it said an employer's statutory contribution cannot simply be treated as an employee deduction merely by describing it as part of CTC.While the move will likely increase compliance costs for small and medium enterprises, the potential costs due to the rise in the wage ceiling can be partly offset by the incentive of up to Rs 3,000 per month for every additional employment created under PM Viksit Bharat Rojgar Yojana.

Article Title: Lung cancer deaths down 16% with low-dose CT screening: IARC
Article Text:
Lung cancer deaths can be reduced through low-dose CT screening, which can also help detect the disease before it reaches advanced stages in people at high risk, according to an IARC assessment.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Low-dose computed tomography (CT) screening can cut the risk of dying from lung cancer by 16% in high-risk people, while also reducing the incidence of advanced stage III or IV disease, an International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) working group has found.Published in The New England Journal of Medicine, the assessment found established evidence that low-dose CT reduces lung cancer mortality when used in people at high risk based mainly on age and smoking history.IARC convened a working group of 23 clinicians and scientists from 17 countries, including Dr Abhishek Shankar of All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi, to assess the benefits and harms of lung cancer screening.The evidence mainly applies to people aged 50 to 80 with a substantial smoking history, typically at least 20 to 30 pack-years. Studies involving former smokers generally included those who had quit within the previous 10 to 15 years, with screening usually performed annually.In India, people aged 50 to 80 with at least 20 pack-years of smoking who are current smokers or quit within the past 15 years can contact the Indian Lung Screening Trial, led by Dr Abhishek Shankar at AIIMS, New Delhi, about screening.Dr Shankar has invited eligible people to contact him for screening under the trial.The evidence behind the finding came mainly from randomised trials. In the US National Lung Screening Trial, people screened with low-dose CT had a 16% lower relative risk of dying from lung cancer than those screened with chest X-rays at seven years. The European NELSON trial also found lower lung cancer mortality among men screened with low-dose CT at 10 years.Based on this evidence, the IARC group classified low-dose CT as Group A, indicating established evidence that it reduces lung cancer mortality and the incidence of stage III or IV disease. Chest X-rays, with or without sputum examination, were classified as Group C, as their ability to reduce lung cancer mortality could not be established.However, the review cautioned that low-dose CT screening is not meant for everyone. False-positive results ranged from 1% to 42% across studies, depending on the screening protocol. Among those with false-positive results, 5% to 32% underwent at least one invasive procedure, with complications occurring in 10% to 22% of such procedures.The review also estimated that 3% to 26% of lung cancers detected in randomised trials involving high-risk people could represent overdiagnosis, meaning cancers that might not have caused harm during the person's lifetime.The working group said effective lung cancer screening needs more than CT scanners, including systems for identifying eligible people, assessing risk, monitoring nodules, providing treatment and follow-up, along with smoking-cessation support. Organised programmes also require trained staff, quality assurance, adequate healthcare capacity and equitable access.
Article Summary: Low-dose computed tomography (CT) screening can cut the risk of dying from lung cancer by 16% in high-risk people. It can also reduce the incidence of advanced stage III or IV disease, according to an IARC assessment. The evidence mainly applies to people aged 50 to 80 with a substantial smoking history.

Article Title: No road agency, contractor penalised for death, disability due to design failures
Article Text:
Faulty road design can turn an everyday drive into a deadly crash.

NEW DELHI: Even seven years after a penal provision was introduced to hold road contractors, designers and road-owning agencies accountable for crashes caused by faulty road design, construction or maintenance resulting in death or disability of victims, not a single agency has been penalised so far under this provision of Motor Vehicles Act Last week experts flagged this issue at a conference on the impact of amendments that govt made to the Motor Vehicles Act in 2019 while pointing out the need to carry out detailed and proper investigation into all serious crashes across all types of roads. However, there have been few instances where agencies and courts have pulled up road owning entities for failure on their part for serious crashes.Only this year, govt increased the penalty for agencies found responsible in such cases by 50 times -- from earlier provision of up to Rs 1 lakh “fine” to up to Rs 50 lakh “penalty” through an amendment to Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act.While fines can be imposed by courts after trial, which is a lengthy process, penalties can be levied directly by administrative, regulatory, or governing authorities for non-compliance without a court trial. Sources said this change is likely to have its impact on govt authorities taking action against agencies responsible for poor design, construction and maintenance where these factors resulted in a serious crash.Some officials of the state road owning agencies admitted that one of the biggest hurdles is establishing a direct causal link between a road engineering defect and a crash as in almost all cases multiple reasons contribute to accidents. This has resulted in accountability remaining confined largely to drivers, with agencies responsible for planning, constructing and maintaining roads escaping scrutiny.The MV Act amendments in 2019 specified that while imposing the fine, courts must consider the road’s design, expected traffic, applicable maintenance standards, the condition in which users could reasonably expect to find the road, whether the designated authority knew or should have known about the hazardous condition, and whether adequate warning signs had been displayed.
Article Summary: Not a single agency has been penalised so far under this provision of Motor Vehicles Act. Only this year, govt increased the penalty for agencies found responsible in such cases by 50 times. Some officials of the state road owning agencies admitted that one of the biggest hurdles is establishing a direct causal link between road engineering defect and a crash.

Article Title: Despite rainfall deficit, kharif acreage above 5-year average
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Overall acreage of kharif (summer-sown) crops in the country declined by just over 1% this year compared with last year and while the dip was expected due to deficient monsoon rainfall this year, the sowing season still ended up recording higher than 'normal' (average of last five years) acreage. Though only marginally above the 'normal', it reflects tweaks in farmers' strategy if warning comes in advance.Latest acreage data shows total sown area at 1,107 lakh hectares (ha) as of Friday was 3 lakh ha more than 'normal' acreage (1,104 lakh ha) despite a cumulative deficit of 12% (June 1-Sept 26) in monsoon rainfall. In the same period in 2025, which recorded 8% more than normal (surplus) rainfall, total acreage was 1,121 lakh ha.The most popular kharif crop and one of the most water-intensive, paddy, reported a 3.6% decline in acreage compared with last year, but this was still 4.6% higher than the 'normal' acreage. Another guzzler, sugarcane, too reported higher acreage than its normal sown area, reflecting farmers' preference for crops which assure them of better returns, even as they had to depend on excessive use of groundwater, at the risk of high input cost.The real test of what rainfall deficit will entail, however, may be reflected in the yield of these crops, first estimates for which will soon be released by the Union agriculture ministry. The output of pulses (mainly pigeon peas), oilseeds (mainly soybean and groundnut), cotton and coarse cereals (mainly bajra and maize) may be a real concern due to deficient and skewed distribution of rainfall in the 'monsoon core zone' - the large part of central India and Bihar which depend on seasonal rains for farming in absence of adequate irrigation coverage.Floods in certain parts of Bihar and Assam, and drought in parts of Maharashtra and Karnataka may also negatively impact the overall output.Apprehending the impact of deficient monsoon rainfall on the rabi (winter-sown) crops due to low moisture content in the soil and shortage of water for irrigation, the agriculture ministry will discuss contingency measures at a two-day meet starting Monday.
Article Summary: Overall acreage of kharif (summer-sown) crops in the country declined by just over 1% this year compared with last year. The dip was expected due to deficient monsoon rainfall this year. But the sowing season still ended up recording higher than 'normal' (average of last five years) acreage.

Article Title: 'Use lowest effective dose of Nsaids': Fresh advisory on kidney risks of painkiller abuse
Article Text:
Health Ministry warns against misuse of painkillers, antibiotics over kidney disease risk.

NEW DELHI: Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) has issued a fresh advisory on rational consumption of painkillers and antibiotics, in view of their repeated use, without proper medical advice, putting people at the risk of kidney complications and other adverse effects.The drug regulator's circular says non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (Nsaids) and antibiotics are prescription medicines under Drugs and Cosmetics Rules and should be used only when clinically indicated, at the appropriate dose and duration and under medical supervision. It has asked people not to take Nsaids, commonly used as painkillers, repeatedly or for a prolonged period without advice.Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation has also cautioned against self-medication with antibiotics and advised people with existing kidney disease or other risk factors for renal impairment to inform their doctor before taking Nsaids.Prof Sandeep Mahajan, nephrologist at AIIMS, said unregulated and prolonged use of painkillers can accelerate the decline in kidney function. "All prescription medicines should be taken under the supervision of a qualified physician, with the prescribed dose and duration strictly followed."CDSCO has advised doctors to use the lowest effective dose of Nsaids for the shortest appropriate duration, with extra caution in patients at risk of kidney injury. This comes against the backdrop of a substantial chronic kidney disease burden in India. A 2025 review of community-based studies estimated pooled chronic kidney disease prevalence at 13.24%, although estimates varied widely across regions and studies.
Article Summary: Health Ministry warns against misuse of painkillers, antibiotics over kidney disease risk. Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation has also cautioned against self-medication with antibiotics. Prof Sandeep Mahajan, nephrologist at AIIMS, said unregulated and prolonged use of painkiller can accelerate the decline in kidney function.

Article Title: Karnataka flags drug landing cost-MRP gap at hospitals of up to 52.6 times; seeks Centre's intervention
Article Text:
Concerns have been raised over critical-care medicines, oncology medicine, high-value injectables, implants and surgical supplies, besides diagnostic-linked consumables and disposable devices.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: Karnataka Food Safety and Drug Administration commissioner K Srinivas has sought urgent regulatory intervention over the pricing of medicines, medical devices and consumables supplied to hospitals at discounted institutional prices but billed to in-patients at the printed maximum retail price (MRP) or close to it.In some cases the difference between the landing cost and MRP is as high as 52 times. In a letter to the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) and the Department of Pharmaceuticals, Srinivas has flagged critical-care medicines, oncology medicine, high-value injectables, implants and surgical supplies, besides diagnostic-linked consumables and disposable devices. The letter says the practice “may be especially harmful” in these categories.Tens of examples have been enclosed with the letter, showing substantial differences between the reported landing cost and MRP of several products.Some with massive margins are: Gufipol, manufactured by Criticare, has a landing cost of Rs 86 and an MRP of Rs 4,528, a difference of 5,165.1%, or 52.6 times the landing cost. Guficycline-50 injection, manufactured by GUFI, has a landing cost of Rs 160 and an MRP of Rs 7,110, a 4,343.7% difference or 44.4 times the landing cost.Terlitis has a landing cost of Rs 118 against an MRP of Rs 4,416, a 3,642.4% difference or 37.4 times.Among the cancer drugs listed, Taxocare 120 mg from Intas has a landing cost of Rs 1,000 and an MRP of Rs 21,617.6, a 2,061.8% difference or 21.6 times. Romy 250 mcg injection, also from Intas, has a landing cost of Rs 1,650 and an MRP of Rs 4,109, a 149% difference or 2.5 times.The commissioner said a recurring pattern had been reported in hospital procurement and billing: a manufacturer or importer supplies an item to a hospital at a very low institutional price, while the pack carries a substantially higher retail MRP. The hospital then supplies it to an in-patient and charges the MRP or a nominal discount on it despite the lower acquisition price.“The patient, who is generally unable to obtain an immediate substitute during admission, bears the entire benefit of the manufacturer-hospital discount being retained within the supply chain,” the letter says.Srinivas described the issue as an “information-asymmetry and captive-patient problem”, saying patients generally do not know the institutional acquisition cost and do not have an effective choice at the point of use.The letter argues that MRP-only regulation is insufficient. “MRP operates as a ceiling on retail sale to a consumer, but it does not by itself ensure that the MRP is a fair patient-facing price in an institutional setting,” it says.It proposes mandatory disclosure of institutional transaction prices, a patient-facing price ceiling linked to acquisition cost, anti-evasion provisions, MRP rationalisation and an enforceable reporting and penalty framework.Under the proposed system, the patient-facing price would be the lowest of the applicable statutory ceiling or notified retail price, the printed MRP, and the net institutional acquisition cost plus a prescribed maximum service margin and applicable taxes.The letter also proposes disclosure on hospital bills of the product details, MRP, net institutional acquisition cost, permitted service margin, taxes and final amount charged. It seeks quarterly electronic reporting, risk-based audits, a grievance channel and refunds with interest where overcharging is established.Srinivas has also sought an expert working group and amendments to the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013, and asked that the matter be treated as “urgent” with a reasoned action taken report communicated.
Article Summary: In some cases the difference between the landing cost and MRP is as high as 52 times. Concerns raised over critical-care medicines, oncology medicine, high- value injectables, implants and surgical supplies. Karnataka Food Safety and Drug Administration commissioner K Srinivas has sought urgent regulatory intervention.

Article Title: IndiGo A321 suffers tail strike during go around at Bangalore; plane lands safely in second attempt
Article Text:
(Representative Image): IndiGo spokesperson said 6E 6542 “experienced an ‘abnormal runway contact’ while landing during gusty weather at Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru. All customers and crew are safe and have disembarked safely.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In yet another instance of an IndiGo Airbus A321 tail strike, an aircraft (VT-NHP) operating a Guwahati-Bengaluru flight on Sunday suffered the same while going around at its destination. The flight (6E 6542) aborted landing on the first approach at the destination. During ascent, it suffered a tail strike. The aircraft landed safely on the second attempt. The DGCA is probing this latest tail strike.IndiGo spokesperson said 6E 6542 “experienced an ‘abnormal runway contact’ while landing during gusty weather at Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru. All customers and crew are safe and have disembarked safely. In line with standard operating procedures, all relevant authorities were informed, and the aircraft is undergoing maintenance checks. It will resume operations after securing necessary clearances. As always, the safety of our customers and crew is our top priority.”The DGCA has raised this issue with IndiGo, and the airline has told it that the focus on pilot training for this particular area has been enhanced.About a year back, they used to happen mostly during landings. Now they are seen more during go-arounds. Airbus itself says, “There is also a higher risk of tail strike when a go-around is required near the ground.”UK’s Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau says the “rate of tail strike incidents per aircraft landing for the A321 is four times greater than that for the A320, probably as a result of the smaller margin from the normal flare attitude. Damage to the structural integrity of the fuselage should not pose a significant flight risk to the aircraft provided the tail strike is detected during or after landing.”An Airbus publication on safety says: “Performing a go-around near the ground is a very dynamic phase with a risk of tail strike. If a go-around is initiated, the (required) manoeuvre must be completed. Between Jan 2022 and Sept 2024, 49 tail strike events were reported to Airbus, with five (10%) during takeoff, 23 (47%) during landing and 21 (43%) during a go-around near the ground.”Tail strikes are a global phenomenon. According to the International Air Transport Association (IATA) Safety Report, tail strikes were the most frequent type of incident in 2024 and in 2025, although fatality risk remains low. IATA data shows tail strikes were the most frequent non-fatal incidents globally at nine, followed by landing gear issues at seven and runway excursion at six.“The ATR 72 and Boeing 737NG (-800/-900ER) were most frequently involved, accounting for 46% of events. Most tail strikes occurred during landing (69% when including rejected landings). Asia Pacific recorded the highest number of events, with the US, India, and Brazil among the most affected countries,” says the IATA Annual Safety Report - 2025.
Article Summary: An IndiGo Airbus A321 tail strike occurred on a Guwahati-Bengaluru flight. The flight (6E 6542) aborted landing on the first approach at the destination. During ascent, it suffered a tail strike. The aircraft landed safely on the second attempt.

Article Title: From 39th to 10th, India breaks into WorldSkills top league
Article Text:
India’s rise has been steady. From 39th in London in 2011, it improved to 33rd in Leipzig in 2013, 29th in São Paulo in 2015 and 19th in Abu Dhabi in 2017.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SHANGHAI: Fifteen years ago, India stood 39th in a global competition that tests whether young people can actually make, repair, design, build and deliver to international occupational standards. On Sunday, it broke into the top 10 for the first time. More telling than the jump itself was where the results came from — bakery and dental prosthetics to digital design, logistics and retail — signalling a skills base widening beyond India’s traditional trades.India finished 10th at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 with six silver medals and 20 Medals for Excellence, improving from its 13th-place finish at Lyon in 2024, where it had won four bronze medals and 12 Medals for Excellence. China topped the Shanghai standings, followed by Korea and Chinese Taipei.India’s six silvers came through Smriti Nambiar in Bakery, Mohammed Salam in Dental Prosthetics, Kovid Ajay Gangrade in Digital Interactive Media Design, Parth Vohra in Industrial Design Technology, Mehrunissa Begum in Logistics and Freight Forwarding and Saniya Joshi in Retail Sales. Nambiar was also named India’s Best of the Nation competitor.Three of the silvers — Dental Prosthetics, Digital Interactive Media Design and Retail Sales — came in categories India entered for the first time, making the performance significant beyond the medal count. India debuted in 11 disciplines in Shanghai, including unmanned aerial systems, intelligent security technology, software testing, aircraft maintenance and optoelectronic technology.Another 20 Medals for Excellence came across a wide spread of occupations, including mechatronics, autonomous mobile robotics, Industry 4.0, additive manufacturing, robot systems integration, automobile technology, chemical laboratory technology, jewellery, fashion technology and health and social care. The medallions are awarded to competitors who demonstrate a high level of professional proficiency against WorldSkills standards.India’s rise has been steady. From 39th in London in 2011, it improved to 33rd in Leipzig in 2013, 29th in São Paulo in 2015 and 19th in Abu Dhabi in 2017. Kazan 2019 brought a breakthrough to 13th and India’s first WorldSkills gold. After again finishing 13th at Lyon, Shanghai has now taken India into the top 10.The scale of India’s participation has expanded too. Its largest-ever contingent of 70 competitors took part across 63 skills, spanning advanced manufacturing, engineering, digital technologies, creative industries and specialised services.Congratulating the team, minister of state for skill development and entrepreneurship Jayant Chaudhary said: “Team India’s remarkable performance at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026, with 6 Silver Medals and 20 Medallions for Excellence, marks a significant leap in our global skills journey. Surpassing our previous performance, our young competitors have demonstrated the growing strength and competitiveness of India’s skilled talent. I congratulate every competitor, expert, trainer and industry partner who contributed to this achievement. Beyond the medals, what makes us proud is the confidence, determination and excellence with which our youth represented India on the world stage. Their success reinforces our commitment to building a future-ready skilling ecosystem and giving every young Indian the opportunity to compete with the best in the world.”Manisha Sensarma, official delegate, WorldSkills India and senior economic adviser in the ministry, said the value of the competition extended beyond medals. “WorldSkills is as much about learning as it is about competing. Shanghai has given our competitors and experts invaluable exposure to evolving global occupational standards, new technologies and international best practices. Our focus now is to translate these learnings into stronger training methodologies, improved assessment standards and deeper industry engagement, so that the benefits of this experience extend well beyond the competition to India’s larger skilling ecosystem.That may be the larger significance of India’s 10th-place finish. Shanghai shows that its best young trainees can increasingly compete across a much wider spectrum of occupations. The next test is whether the standards, training practices and industry exposure behind that performance can be translated into improvements across the country’s broader skilling ecosystem.
Article Summary: India finished 10th at WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 with six silver medals and 20 Medals for Excellence. China topped the Shanghai standings, followed by Korea and Chinese Taipei. India debuted in 11 disciplines in Shanghai, including unmanned aerial systems, intelligent security technology and software testing.

Article Title: NEET leak fallout: CISF to guard NTA’s confidential exam areas
Article Text:
(Representative image): CISF will carry out access-control and screening measures, including frisking with X-ray baggage screening machines and Door Frame Metal Detectors (DFMDs).

NTA shifts sensitive operations to new office

Cybersecurity measures being strengthened

Paper leak exposed gaps in confidential section

Earlier reforms and fresh scrutiny

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The National Testing Agency (NTA) has tightened security around its examination work with 39 CISF personnel deployed at its New Delhi office. The force will monitor confidential areas, control access and screen staff and visitors. The move follows repeated questions over paper leaks and administrative lapses, including the handling of sensitive examination material.The CISF personnel have been deployed at entry and exit points of the confidential areas at the Government of India Press Building on Minto Road. They will carry out access-control and screening measures, including frisking with X-ray baggage screening machines and Door Frame Metal Detectors (DFMDs).The NTA has also demarcated confidential areas within its new premises. Movement and operations in these areas will be closely monitored as part of efforts to prevent unauthorised access to examination material."Confidential areas have been demarcated in the building where the movement and operations will be strictly monitored to ensure that a foolproof system is in place. The Home Ministry has approved Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) security cover for the premises," a senior official said.The security measures come after the NTA moved its confidential and sensitive operations from its earlier office in Okhla to a new facility on Minto Road."A dedicated over 55,000 square feet office space has been allotted in the Government of India Press Building on Minto Road. The fifth floor and parts of the fourth and sixth floors of the said building have been allotted to the National Testing Agency. Confidential and sensitive operations have been shifted in the last one month to the newly allotted building," the official said.Other parts of the Government of India Press Building are already protected by the CISF. The NTA will now have a dedicated security arrangement for its examination-related confidential areas.The agency's new security framework also includes tighter monitoring of examination-critical technology systems. The NTA is working on strict access controls, encryption standards, immutable logging and tamper-evident storage."Arrangements are being made in mission mode for establishing strict access controls, encryption standards, immutable logging and tamper-evident storage for all examination-critical workloads."The NTA is also reviewing the security of systems used throughout the examination cycle. These include candidate registration, fee payment, admit cards, computer-based testing, OMR processing, result systems and other examination-supporting infrastructure."Running security readiness reviews of all examination-supporting systems before each examination cycle in coordination with NTA's technology function and coordinating with NTA's test-security function on the technical security of examination day workflows -- including biometric authentication, face-matching, CCTV systems and live monitoring infrastructure -- are among the action items being worked upon," the official said.The agency is also preparing an examination-specific cyber-incident response system. It plans to have enhanced security operations centre monitoring and rapid-response capabilities on examination days.The NTA has designated a dedicated chief information security officer (CISO) to oversee information security."The position of general manager and CISO has been advertised, and the selection process is at an advanced stage. Independent third-party cyber-security audits by CERT-In and C-DAC empanelled agencies continue to be undertaken," the official said.The latest security measures follow the 2024 NEET-UG paper leak, which triggered nationwide student protests and brought scrutiny on the NTA's examination processes.A CBI chargesheet identified three subject experts as the primary sources of the leaked paper. According to the chargesheet, experts entering the NTA's confidential section were not checked or frisked during entry or exit.The experts were allegedly able to take briefs from the question papers on small chits made from plain sheets provided to them for rough work and translation.The CBI also noted that the NTA did not have a dedicated CCTV live-feed monitoring control room in its Delhi office. This meant the activities of the three accused experts went unnoticed.The NTA was established in 2017 under the Ministry of Education to conduct fair, transparent and standardised examinations.The 2024 NEET paper leak had also led to the setting up of a high-level committee headed by former ISRO chairman K Radhakrishnan. The panel recommended stronger security controls across the examination process.Its recommendations covered question paper systems, candidate registration, fee payment, admit cards, computer-based testing platforms, OMR processing, normalisation engines and result systems.A separate high-powered task force headed by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani was also announced to recommend reforms to make the examination system leakproof. The panel was set up after the controversy and is yet to submit its report.Following the 2026 paper leak, the Supreme Court reprimanded the NTA, saying "it has not learnt its lessons".The latest security overhaul therefore extends beyond physical protection of confidential material. The agency is now combining CISF security, tighter access controls, CCTV and live monitoring with cybersecurity audits and technical safeguards across its examination systems.
Article Summary: The National Testing Agency (NTA) has tightened security around its examination work with 39 CISF personnel deployed at its New Delhi office. The force will monitor confidential areas, control access and screen staff and visitors. The move follows repeated questions over paper leaks and administrative lapses.

Article Title: Kapil Sibal alleges ‘unilateral’ EC decisions, seeks action against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
Article Text:
Kapil Sibal alleges ‘unilateral’ EC decisions, seeks action against CEC Gyanesh Kumar

Sibal alleges unilateral decision-making

EC responds to concerns over SIR and electoral rolls

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Rajya Sabha member Kapil Sibal on Sunday escalated the political row over the Election Commission 's Special Intensive Revision (SIR), accusing chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of taking "unilateral decisions" and demanding his removal from office.Sibal also urged the Supreme Court to examine the Election Commission's records, dissent notes and orders issued during the period under question, and consider nullifying elections conducted during the 10-month period he referred to.The former Union minister's remarks came amid a controversy over internal objections raised by election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi regarding decisions related to electoral rolls, the EC's IT systems and the SIR exercise.According to Sibal, the Election Commission's own statement issued on Saturday acknowledged that decisions had not been taken unanimously over the past several months. He alleged that Kumar had taken decisions "unilaterally" rather than through the full three-member Commission.Sibal claimed that Commission meetings were conducted without agendas being circulated or minutes being recorded, preventing the other commissioners from reviewing or commenting on decisions.He said the alleged practices covered 10 months, including elections held in Bihar in June 2025 and West Bengal in April.The allegations follow a report by The Indian Express, which said Sandhu and Joshi had formally raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders that they said were issued without their knowledge.Sibal also alleged that decisions concerning additions and deletions of voters were centralised in Delhi through ECI NET under Seema Khanna, who managed its operations, instead of being handled by statutory Electoral Registration Officers.He demanded that an FIR be registered against Khanna and that she be arrested, arguing that unlike the CEC, she does not have statutory immunity from criminal prosecution.Sibal also alleged that changes were made to Form 6, used for new voter registration, requiring details of parents or grandparents without the central government issuing the required notification.The Election Commission on Saturday announced several decisions addressing issues that Sandhu and Joshi had raised in their internal communications.On Form 6, the EC said the additional declaration requiring new voters to provide details of their own or their parents' or grandparents' entries in the electoral roll from the previous SIR had been upheld by the Supreme Court.It said the additional requirement was specific to the SIR exercise and that regular statutory forms would continue to be used outside an SIR.On access to electoral-roll databases, the EC said field officers have role-based access to ECINET according to their statutory powers. It also announced a review by a committee headed by a senior deputy election commissioner and including an independent IIT or IIIT expert to "double-check" the system's compliance with election laws and rules.The Commission further said agendas for all meetings would be circulated in advance and minutes issued, while directions issued by commissioners to EC officers would be complied with.On the IT division, the EC said disputed changes in the distribution of work were never implemented after Sandhu and Joshi intervened, and that oversight of the division by the deputy election commissioner was never withdrawn.Sibal, however, claimed that the alleged irregularities meant elections conducted from Bihar through West Bengal during the period were "illegal". He called on the Supreme Court to take suo motu cognisance of the matter and consider whether recent elections should be annulled.The opposition has also demanded Kumar's removal and an independent review of decisions and electoral-roll changes made during his tenure.
Article Summary: Rajya Sabha member Kapil Sibal accuses chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of taking "unilateral decisions" and demanding his removal from office. Sibal also urged the Supreme Court to examine the Election Commission's records, dissent notes and orders issued during the period under question, and consider nullifying elections.
