Article Title: Jason and Kylie Kelce’s latest $2.9 billion market move marks a new milestone as their investment reaches 5,000+ stores
Article Text:
Jason and Kylie Kelce’s latest $2.9 billion market move marks a new milestone as their investment reaches 5,000+ stores

Jason Kelce backs a brand he already knew well

New Heights

Hank Sauce has already reached more than 5,000 stores

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jason Kelce is expanding his post-NFL business portfolio, with his latest move taking him into the growing hot sauce market. Through Winnie Capital, the family office supporting the business and philanthropic activities of Jason and Kylie Kelce, a strategic equity investment has been made in Hank Sauce, the Sea Isle City, New Jersey-based brand that has grown from a local favorite into a product sold in thousands of stores. The deal gives Hank Sauce another major name behind its plans for wider national distribution while also adding a growing consumer brand to the Kelces’ business interests.Hank Sauce announced the strategic equity investment from Winnie Capital on December 22, 2025. Neither side disclosed the financial terms, meaning the amount invested and the size of the equity stake remain private.Kelce’s connection to Hank Sauce, however, goes beyond the investment. The former Philadelphia Eagles center has spent considerable time around South Jersey over the years and was already familiar with Hank Sauce and its Sea Isle City restaurant before the business relationship developed.According to reporting surrounding the deal, Winnie Capital formally connected with the Hank Sauce founders in September 2024. That eventually developed into the investment announced more than a year later.This distinction is important. Kelce is not simply appearing in an advertising campaign for the company. Winnie Capital has taken an equity position in the existing business, while Jason is also expected to contribute to brand awareness, content and marketing as Hank Sauce attempts to reach a larger audience.Kylie Kelce is connected to the deal through Winnie Capital, which serves as the family office for the couple’s business and philanthropic activities. The announcement does not disclose a separate personal investment from Kylie, so her role is more accurately described through the family’s investment operation.Jason also brings something that cannot be measured simply by the undisclosed investment figure. After 13 NFL seasons with the Eagles and a growing media career that includes thepodcast with Travis Kelce, he has an audience that can introduce Hank Sauce to consumers far beyond its Jersey Shore base.Winnie Capital is investing in a company that has already spent years building its business.Brian “Hank” Ruxton, Matt Pittaluga and Josh Jaspan founded Hank Sauce in 2011. The business started on a much smaller scale before gradually expanding its production, restaurant operation and retail distribution.Hank Sauce now says its products are available in more than 5,000 retail locations nationwide. Its distribution includes retailers such as Publix, GIANT, ACME, ShopRite, Sprouts, Cabela’s and Ace Hardware, giving the company a footprint that already stretches well beyond New Jersey.The business also operates from a 10,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Millville, New Jersey, a major change from its early years when production was considerably smaller and bottles were made by hand.Its Sea Isle City restaurant, meanwhile, dates back to 2012 and remains an important part of the company’s connection to the Jersey Shore.The product itself was built around a straightforward idea. Rather than competing only on extreme heat, Hank Sauce has focused heavily on flavor. That approach has allowed the company to appeal to customers who enjoy hot sauce without necessarily looking for the hottest product possible.Winnie Capital investment comes as Hank Sauce targets a much bigger marketHank Sauce is trying to expand in a sizeable category. The U.S. hot sauce market has been valued at roughly $2.9 billion, according to market figures cited in reporting surrounding Kelce’s investment.The opportunity for Hank Sauce is therefore much larger than its original Jersey Shore customer base.The company already has several pieces needed for further expansion, including its own production facility, more than 5,000 retail locations, an established product lineup and over a decade of operating history. The next challenge is increasing national recognition while continuing to add retailers, restaurants and other distribution channels.That is where Winnie Capital’s investment and Jason Kelce’s involvement could play a role. Along with providing capital, the partnership is expected to include work around content, marketing and brand visibility.For Kylie Kelce, the deal is connected to the broader activities of the family office she shares with Jason rather than a separately announced personal investment. For Jason, it gives him an equity interest through Winnie Capital in a company he was already familiar with as a consumer.Hank Sauce has now been operating for around 15 years, has expanded into more than 5,000 stores and produces its sauces from a 10,000-square-foot New Jersey facility. With Winnie Capital now holding an equity stake, the next stage of the company’s story will center on whether a brand built along the Jersey Shore can turn that existing footprint into a much larger national presence.
Article Summary: Hank Sauce announced the strategic equity investment from Winnie Capital on December 22, 2025. Neither side disclosed the financial terms, meaning the amount invested and the size of the equity stake remain private. Jason Kelce is not simply appearing in an advertising campaign for the company. He is expected to contribute to brand awareness, content and marketing.

Article Title: Are banks open or closed today? Why 3-day bank strike was deferred by unions; what customers should know
Article Text:
The UFBU agreed to defer the agitation programmes and strike actions that had been planned, its statement said.

Why bank unions deferred strike

Why were bank unions planning to strike & what assurances have they got?

What bank unions said earlier

On which days are banks open this week?

Bank customers dreading a delay in transactions due to the proposed three-day bank strike have reason to cheer as the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) has decided to defer the move.This means that all banks across the country will continue to function as usual for the strike period that had been announced September 28-30. This also assumes significance since it's the time for half yearly closing.Bank unions on Sunday called off their planned three-day nationwide strike after the Indian Banks' Association (IBA) gave assurances on their key demands, including the long-pending demand for a five-day working week.The strike, which was scheduled to begin on Monday, had been announced by the United Forum of Bank Unions. The proposed industrial action also coincided with the half-yearly closing period.Following the developments and the assurances given on the issues related to the strike, the UFBU agreed to defer the agitation programmes and strike actions that had been planned, its statement said.With the strike deferred, bank branches will remain operational on Monday.Under the understanding reached between the unions and the IBA, a high-level committee comprising representatives of both sides will be constituted immediately to examine the demand for declaring the remaining Saturdays as holidays."A high-level committee of the IBA and UFBU will be formed immediately to deliberate on the issue of declaring the remaining Saturdays as holidays. This committee will explore all possible alternatives, discuss with all the stakeholders, and work out a solution acceptable to all the stakeholders, more importantly, the customers," the UFBU said in a statement, according to PTI.The two sides will also take up the Performance Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme applicable to Scale IV and above officers.Discussions with the IBA can begin on possible changes to the scheme, which can then be proposed to the government after taking into account the concerns raised by the unions and associations, the UFBU said.The unions and the IBA will also discuss the remaining issues mentioned in the minutes dated March 8, 2024, with the aim of resolving them at the earliest, it said.Earlier, the UFBU had announced a three-day nationwide strike. This had compelled banks to issue advisories to customers to complete their important banking transactions in advance. Some banks had even remained open on Sunday on the Finance Ministry and RBI’s directions.Narendra Sharma, UFBU Himachal Pradesh Convenor and President of the Bankers United Forum of Himachal Pradesh, had said the unions had been pushed towards industrial action because commitments contained in an agreement with the government, signed more than two-and-a-half years ago, had still not been implemented.“Our main demand is the implementation of a five-day banking week, with Saturday and Sunday as weekly holidays. The second major issue is the withdrawal of the new Performance Linked Incentive scheme, which has been implemented unilaterally by the Department of Financial Services. More than two-and-a-half years have passed since the agreement was signed, but the commitments made in it have still not been implemented. We have therefore been left with no option but to resort to agitation,” said Sharma.With the September 28-30 bank strike being called off, banks across the country will remain open for five days this week. This is due to a national holiday on Friday, October 2, on account of Gandhi Jayanti. Since October 3 will be the first Saturday of the month, banks will remain open.October is a month of festivals across the country and several holidays are lined up depending on the state and region. Customers may do well to check their state-specific bank holiday list.
Article Summary: The United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) has decided to defer the move. This means that all banks across the country will continue to function as usual for the strike period that had been announced September 28-30. This also assumes significance since it's the time for half yearly closing.

Article Title: SC refuses interim stay on MDR for UPI transactions, but asks Centre to explain decision
Article Text:
SC asks ‘what is the service’ behind new charges

Mobile retailers plan 'No UPI Day'

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has issued notice to the Centre, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) on a plea challenging Gazette notifications introducing charges on commercial UPI transactions above Rs 2,000.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing a writ petition filed by advocate Anjan Datta challenging Gazette notifications issued by the Union Ministry of Finance on September 14 and 15.The court directed the Centre and other respondents to file their counter affidavits within four weeks, while observing that the issue was “less legal and more technical”."Is it tax or a fee? If not a fee, what is the executive basis for making this expropriation? What is the service?" Justice Bagchi said."269 permits a transfer...if it permits transfer, so cash from one assessee moves to another, then what is the character of receipt. In UPI who gets it? We are not on the [coverage]. We are on legal incidence. What is the source of legal incidence of this?" Bagchi said.The court, however, declined to stay the Centre’s decision to impose merchant discount rate (MDR) on specified person-to-merchant UPI transactions above Rs 2,000.The charges are set to take effect from October 15.The Centre told the Supreme Court that 96 per cent of people using payment gateways would be exempt from the MDR on UPI payments above Rs 2,000.The plea has been filed against the Union government, the RBI, NPCI and the UPI & Services Steering Committee. The petitioner has contended that imposing charges on commercial UPI transactions could have a wider impact on the public, as businesses may pass the additional costs on to consumers.The Union government has introduced a framework allowing MDR charges on specified high-value commercial UPI transactions while retaining free UPI payments for individuals and small merchants. The move follows amendments to the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, and notifications issued by the Ministry of Finance in September 2026.The Supreme Court hearing comes as mobile phone retailers across India are set to observe October 2 as “No UPI Day” to protest the 0.4 per cent MDR on eligible UPI transactions, a senior official of the All India Mobile Retailers Association (AIMRA) said.“The All India Mobile Retailers Association (AIMRA) has called for a 'NO UPI DAY' on October 2, 2026, to highlight the concerns of mobile retailers regarding the 0.4 per cent Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) applicable to eligible merchant UPI transactions,” AIMRA Vice President and President for Delhi NCR region, Tarvinder Singh, said in a statement.Singh said retailers would symbolically cover their UPI QR codes with black cloth and refrain from accepting UPI payments on Gandhi Jayanti.In a representation to finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman, AIMRA said the MDR would result in an immediate net monthly loss of Rs 2,000 to Rs 12,000 for a small retailer processing Rs 5 lakh to Rs 30 lakh a month through UPI, substantially reducing their net income.The retailers’ body estimated that the 0.4 per cent MDR would impose a burden of around Rs 40 crore per month and nearly Rs 500 crore annually on small mobile retailers across India.“If We Want Digital India, UPI Must Remain Zero MDR. This is not a protest against UPI or Digital India. Our concern is the additional financial burden being placed on merchants who accept digital payments. If we want Digital India to grow further, digital payments should remain affordable for the entire retail ecosystem. Our clear demand is that UPI merchant payments should continue under a Zero MDR structure,” Singh said.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court has issued notice to the Centre, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the National Payments Corporation of India. Mobile phone retailers across India are set to observe October 2 as ‘No UPI Day’ to protest the 0.4 per cent Merchant Discount Rate (MDR)

Article Title: Tenant stayed even after rent agreement expired, but a Rs 25 lakh loan to landlady changed the date of calculation; Delhi HC orders payout of Rs 3.27 crore plus 6% interest as mesne profits
Article Text:
The case took a significant turn in 2007, when the landlady borrowed Rs 25 lakh from the tenant. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about:

The Rs 25 lakh loan angle

Why did the landlady win the case?

You rent out your property and the rent agreement expires, and the tenant does not vacate it, but continues to pay you higher rent. Are you entitled to claim mesne profits, which is a compensation that is payable by a person who has wrongfully possessed someone else’s property for the profits or benefits they actually received, or could reasonably have received, from that possession.A tenant may be asked to pay mesne profits when they remain in possession of a property after the tenancy agreement has expired and the landlord has issued an eviction notice.The Delhi High Court recently this very principle of mesne profits in a case involving a bank, directing the tenant to pay out, along with 6% annual interest, to the landlady for continuing to occupy the premises beyond the agreed tenancy period.A Delhi-based landlady, had rented out a property in Defence Colony Market in 2002. The building consisted of two floors and a terrace, although only the first and second floors were leased to the tenant.The monthly rent was fixed at Rs 62,000. According to the submissions made before the court, the first floor measured 1,600 sq. ft., while the second floor had an area of 1,200 sq. ft.The registered rent agreement began on January 1, 2002, and was valid until December 31, 2004, making the original tenancy period three years.The agreement also contained a provision for a 20% increase in rent if the tenancy was renewed after December 31, 2004, according to an ET report.The agreement, however, was not renewed when the three-year period ended. The tenant neither entered into a fresh agreement nor vacated the premises on January 1, 2005.Instead, it continued occupying the property and paying the increased rent. With the original agreement having expired, the tenancy from that point operated on a month-to-month basis.The tenant eventually remained in possession for several more years and vacated the premises only on December 31, 2017.Before that, in May 2008, the landlady issued a legal notice to the tenant demanding that it vacate the property. She also sought mesne profits of Rs 4 lakh per month from June 2008, until the premises were actually vacated. Despite receiving the notice, the tenant continued to occupy the property.The landlady subsequently approached the court, challenging the tenant's continued occupation of the premises. On July 9, 2026, the Delhi High Court delivered its judgment in the case and directed the tenant to pay the specified mesne profits to the landlady.Asha Kiran Sharma, Partner, King Stubb and Kasiva, told ET that the original rent agreement came to an end on December 31, 2004. Although the agreement contained a renewal provision, the tenant was required to submit a written request for renewal before the existing agreement expired.No such written request was made by the tenant within the stipulated period. As a result, there was no formal renewal of the rent agreement.At the same time, the landlady continued to communicate with the tenant in 2005 and 2007, increasing the rent by 20%, while the tenant continued making payments at the higher rate.Sharma says that the courts interpreted this conduct as an "extension" of the tenancy rather than the creation of a fresh lease meaning the tenant continued as a lawful month-to-month tenant, not a trespasser, even without a registered document."The case took a significant turn in 2007, when the landlady borrowed Rs 25 lakh from the tenant, with her husband acting as the guarantor. As a condition attached to the loan, the landlady signed a notarised undertaking in which she agreed to continue the tenancy until the entire loan had been repaid.The arrangement also provided that the loan EMIs would be adjusted against the rent payable to her. The loan was eventually repaid in May 2012.Despite this commitment, the landlady issued a legal notice in May 2008 seeking to end the tenancy.The court, however, held that the 2008 notice could not supersede the binding undertaking that the landlady had already given, under which she had agreed to allow the tenant to remain in the premises until the loan was cleared. In other words, she could not subsequently withdraw from that commitment.Sharma says that this was the reason the court did not grant mesne profits for the period between 2008 and 2012. During these years, the tenant's occupation continued to be considered authorised under the tenancy arrangement and was therefore not treated as unauthorised possession. The tenant was consequently liable only to pay the agreed rent and not damages.The repayment of the loan in May 2012 became the key event in determining when the tenancy could effectively come to an end. Once the loan had been cleared, the court treated that point as the trigger for termination.The tenant's continued occupation thereafter was considered unauthorised, making it liable for mesne profits calculated at market rates until it eventually vacated the premises in December 2017.This formed the basis of the landlady's successful mesne profits claim in the Delhi High Court's July 9, 2026 judgment.Under the July 2026 order, the tenant was directed to pay mesne profits at Rs 163 per sq. ft. per month for the period from May 2012 to December 2015. From January 2016 until December 31, 2017, the amount was to be calculated with a 15% increase in rent. The order also imposed 6% annual interest. The order will attain finality unless it is challenged before a higher court.Based on ET’s estimated calculations using the Delhi High Court's July 2026 order, the total mesne profits work out to Rs 3,26,78,240, or approximately Rs 3.27 crore. This amount is in addition to the 6% annual interest directed by the court.The landlady subsequently approached the court seeking a review on limited technical grounds. Her review petition was dismissed in September 2026, with the court observing that the attempt was essentially to reopen findings that had already been decided. Such an exercise falls outside the scope of a review petition.
Article Summary: A Delhi-based landlady, had rented out a property in Defence Colony Market in 2002. The rent agreement began on January 1, 2002, and was valid until December 31, 2004, making the original tenancy period three years. The agreement, however, was not renewed when the three-year period ended. The tenant neither entered into a fresh agreement nor vacated the premises. Instead, it continued occupying the property and paying the increased rent. The case took a significant turn in 2007, when theLandlady borrowed Rs 25 lakh from the tenant.

Article Title: A 14-year-old Georgia student scored a perfect 1600 on the SAT after taking college-level courses; Ashrit Talluri of Fulton County achieved the maximum score while still in an age group far younger th
Article Text:
A much earlier start to the SAT

He is already taking college courses

From test preparation to a future in medicine

A 14-year-old student in Georgia has achieved the highest possible score on the SAT, completing a test generally associated with students much further along in high school. Ashrit Talluri of Fulton County earned a perfect 1600 on the exam, according to FOX 5 Atlanta and The Independent, with additional reporting from outlets including Andhra Jyothy confirming his academic background and current studies. The SAT has a maximum score of 1600, made up of Reading and Writing and Math sections, each scored out of 800. College Board data places a 1600 in the 99+ percentile among its comparison groups.Talluri’s academic path had already moved beyond the usual pace before he sat for the exam. While in middle school, he completed 14½ high school credits. That coursework helped him qualify for college-level summer programs at Harvard and Rice.His father and middle school counselor encouraged him to take the SAT, and he registered in January. He then spent about five months preparing, working with a tutor, using online study material and completing more than two dozen practice tests. FOX 5 reported that he had already achieved a 1600 on three practice SATs before taking the official examination.Talluri eventually took the official test in June. The waiting period that followed was particularly significant because his result went through verification before being released.When the score arrived, it showed a perfect 1600.The achievement is notable partly because of Talluri’s age. College Board’s SAT percentile comparisons are based largely on students in grades 11 and 12 or recent graduating classes, while Talluri was only 14 when he took the exam.The SAT result is just one part of Talluri’s academic workload. He is now in ninth grade at Fulton County’s Innovation Academy, where he is taking two college-level courses through dual enrolment. Outside the classroom, he takes part in hackathons around Atlanta and is involved in chess and aviation. His public LinkedIn profile also lists interests in artificial intelligence, medicine, computer science and research.Instead of abandoning the process of preparing for tests after accomplishing his own objectives, Talluri has chosen to continue his engagement with SAT materials. He dedicates a portion of his leisure time to the creation of practice questions and delving into various strategies, all aimed at assisting fellow students in their preparation for the challenging exam.Talluri has said he hopes to become a neurosurgeon, a career that aligns with his interest in both medicine and technology. His public professional profile describes him as a student interested in AI and medical applications, while also listing projects and extracurricular activities connected to those fields.His profile prominently highlights his role as the visionary founder of CerebroAegis, an innovative project dedicated to harnessing smartphone sensors for the potential screening of strokes, as well as offering valuable health-safety support. This initiative is positioned as an advanced AI-driven health technology venture rather than being deemed a replacement for professional medical diagnosis, thereby emphasizing its supportive role in healthcare.Currently, Talluri is navigating the challenges of being a ninth-grade student while simultaneously balancing the rigorous requirements of advanced college-level coursework, alongside active involvement in various extracurricular pursuits and participation in competitive academic events. Despite achieving an impressive perfect SAT score at a notably young age, which many might view as extraordinary, his educational path is still in a dynamic state of progression as he continues to push the boundaries of his academic studies. Looking forward, the forthcoming phase of his academic journey is sure to encompass a similar mix of demanding coursework, a pronounced emphasis on technology-driven interests, and calculated preparations that have already propelled him well past the typical educational timeline.
Article Summary: Ashrit Talluri of Fulton County, Georgia, earned a perfect 1600 on the exam. The SAT has a maximum score of 1600, made up of Reading and Writing and Math sections, each scored out of 800. College Board data places a 1600 in the 99+ percentile among its comparison groups.

Article Title: In 2024, 75-year-old Iowa farmer Evie Haupt said three wind turbines on her 160 acres were bringing in about $35,000 a year while using under 3 acres and had helped reduce $350,000 in farm debt to $67
Article Text:
A financial lifeline for rural landowners

The explosive expansion of Iowa wind power

Addressing local pushback and debate

On a 160-acre farm in central Iowa, three tall wind turbines quietly rise above the fields. Each turbine uses less than an acre of land, but together they provide an annual income that has changed the financial future of 75-year-old farmer Evie Haupt. According to a CBS News report by Janet Shamlian and Alicia Hastey, Haupt earns about $35,000 each year by leasing part of her land for the wind turbines. The income rises with inflation and has helped her pay down a $350,000 farm debt left after her husband died a decade ago. Her remaining debt is now $67,000. For many family farms across the United States, extra sources of income have become important lifelines. The U.S. Department of Agriculture expects farm profits to fall by 25 per cent, as farmers face higher costs, changing crop prices and unpredictable weather. Adding wind power to traditional farming can provide steady income and help protect farmers from financial shocks.Farm debt can leave families with difficult choices, including selling land that has been in the family for generations. Haupt faced this situation after her husband died and left her with hundreds of thousands of dollars in farm debt.Payments from the wind turbines provided her with a regular source of income that she could use to repay the loans. Each turbine takes up less than an acre, allowing Haupt to continue farming most of her 160 acres. This means the same land provides her with two sources of income while only a small portion is used for the turbines. The payments can also increase over time because the contracts include inflation adjustments, helping landowners manage rising prices and other costs. For Haupt, the arrangement has made a significant difference. She has now paid off more than 80% of her farm debt while continuing to use the land for farming.Iowa has become a major wind energy state over the past two decades. According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, Iowa had only a few hundred wind turbines 20 years ago. Today, it has more than 6,000, producing about 60 per cent of the state's energy. Across the United States, more than 70,000 land-based wind turbines are operating, according to the U.S. Department of Energy. Nationwide, wind power supplies about 10 per cent of the electric grid. Federal energy officials also say current U.S. wind power cuts carbon emissions by an amount equal to taking 73 million passenger vehicles off the road. Attorney Kathy Law, who grew up on a farm and married a farmer, has helped place nearly half of Iowa's wind turbines. Her work in energy law grew from her own family's experience with farming. Law wanted to study law while she was in high school, but the severe farm crisis of the 1980s kept her home to help with the family farm. She later went to law school in her forties. She graduated on the same day her son finished high school and later served as president of the Iowa Wind Energy Association for three years. "From my farm background, I think I can talk their talk and have conversations with landowners that are interested in having wind turbines on their property," Law told CBS News.The rapid growth of wind power in rural communities has also brought opposition in some counties. Local critics say wind turbines can change scenic views, create unwanted noise and threaten birds and bats. Law believes landowners should be able to decide what happens on their property. "Nobody's requiring them to put that on their farms or on their land," Law said during her interview with CBS News. "We want to be able to put turbines on our land and receive those benefits. " Haupt has a similar view of the changes to her farm. While she remains attached to traditional farming, she sees clean energy as an important step for rural communities. "I look at it as progress," Haupt told CBS News. "I think we can't stand in the way of progress." For Haupt, giving up a very small part of her land to produce electricity makes sense for her finances and for the wider community. "I need to give up one or two acres of my land so that I can generate a commodity that we all use every day, and we all want to use more of it every day," Haupt said. "So I'm happy to be able to be a part of that generation."
Article Summary: Iowa has become a major wind energy state over the past two decades. More than 70,000 land-based wind turbines are operating in the U.S. Nationwide, wind power supplies about 10 per cent of the electric grid. Critics say wind turbines change scenic views, create unwanted noise and threaten birds and bats.

Article Title: At 21°C, Delhi records its lowest minimum temperature in Sept in 18 years
Article Text:
Last year, Delhi recorded 41% surplus rainfall.

As ‘good’ as it gets: Parts of capital soak in air benefits of Sept showers





NEW DELHI: Delhi’s Sunday recorded its lowest minimum temperature in 18 years — 21 degrees Celsius, three notches below normal.With cool north and north-easterly winds, heavy rain and storm in adjoining states and large parts of northern, central and eastern India, Delhi has been experiencing early winter-like mornings.However, Met expects both minimum and maximum temperatures to gradually rise over the next few days.“The minimum temperature of 21 degrees Celsius recorded at Safdarjung was the second-lowest minimum temperature recorded in the month of Sept since 2001. The lowest was 20.8 degrees Celsius, recorded on Sept 6, 2008, and the third lowest was 21.1 degrees Celsius, on Sept 19, 2024,” said Krishna Mishra, weather scientist at IMD.While Ridge recorded a minimum of 16.8 degrees Celsius, Palam saw 19.2 degrees Celsius and Ayanagar 21.2 degrees Celsius. On Saturday, the minimum temperature was 23.2 degrees Celsius.At base station Safdarjung, the maximum temperature was recorded at 30.6 degrees Celsius, four notches below normal, against 29.2 degrees Celsius a day earlier.The city also saw its air quality improve within the ‘satisfactory’ category.The AQI at 4pm Sunday was 53 — the best air quality Delhi has seen since July 9, when it stood at 48. In many parts, the air quality was recorded in the ‘good’ category.On Monday, the minimum temperature is expected in the 20-22 degrees range while the maximum is likely to hover around 31-33 degrees Celsius. As per Met, no showers are expected from Monday onwards.Met said very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall was recorded due to a deep depression formation over the west-central bay – from Andra Pradesh to Odisha, Chhattisgarh, eastern Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Bihar, UP till Uttarakhand.“A very large area saw intense rain activity, up to more than 30cm at many places in UP. The low minimum temperatures in Delhi and adjoining areas can be attributed to this large-scale rain,” Mishra said, adding that minimum temperature departures in UP, Chhattisgarh and eastern MP are running up to 4 degrees below normal.“The maximum temperature departure on Sunday was up to 10 degrees below normal in parts of UP; 5-7 degrees below normal in parts of Chhattisgarh and MP; and 7-8 degrees below normal in Uttarakhand. Even in Delhi, it was around four notches below normal in some parts,” he said, adding that the weather will soon turn dry, with monsoon withdrawal advancing to parts of UP and Punjab, and beyond.While Delhi saw monsoon retreat on Sept 23, two days before its normal withdrawal, with 728.6mm of rainfall (Safdarjung), which is considered normal and 16% above the average monsoon rainfall of 629.7mm, parts of the city recorded 5mm post-monsoon rainfall Saturday due to the depression and western disturbance feeding additional moisture in the region.Last year, the city recorded 41% surplus rainfall.
Article Summary: With cool north and north-easterly winds, heavy rain and storm in adjoining states and large parts of northern, central and eastern India, Delhi has been experiencing early winter-like mornings. Met expects both minimum and maximum temperatures to gradually rise over the next few days.

Article Title: Vijay launches ‘Thai Maaman’ free gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai
Article Text:
Chief Minister Vijay launches Thai Maaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam in Madurai, handing over free one-gram gold rings to newborn beneficiaries





MADURAI: Chief minister C Joseph Vijay has inaugurated the Thai Maaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam in Madurai, launching a scheme to provide a free one-gram gold ring to newborns in government hospitals.The government said the scheme aims to encourage deliveries in state-run hospitals and strengthen public confidence in government healthcare.Babies born in government hospitals and primary health centres from noon on June 22 are eligible. The bottom line

Bharat NCAP 2.0, planned for October 2027, will look beyond what happens when a car crashes. The proposed system will examine the entire safety chain: from how a vehicle helps avoid a collision to how well it protects occupants, pedestrians and other vulnerable road users, and what happens after an accident.Union road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari announced the proposed timeline at the SIAM Annual Convention in September. The second phase is being planned as the first phase of Bharat New Car Assessment Programme, or Bharat NCAP, approaches the end of its current cycle.According to the ministry of road transport and highways’ draft AIS-197 Revision 1, the first phase of Bharat NCAP began on October 1, 2023 and is valid until September 30, 2027. The draft revision has been prepared as the framework for Bharat NCAP 2.0.The proposed changes could make the safety rating a much broader measure of a car’s performance, not just in a crash, but before, during and after one.Bharat NCAP is India’s own vehicle crash-testing and safety-rating programme. It was formally launched by the ministry of road transport and highways in August 2023 and became operational from October 1, 2023.The programme applies to type-approved passenger vehicles in the M1 category with a gross vehicle weight of less than 3.5 tonnes. It is voluntary, which means manufacturers can offer eligible vehicles for assessment.The programme is anchored by the Central Institute of Road Transport (CIRT), while testing is carried out through designated agencies with the required infrastructure.At its core, Bharat NCAP gives car buyers a common safety benchmark. A vehicle must already meet mandatory regulatory requirements to be sold in India. Bharat NCAP goes a step further by putting eligible vehicles through specified tests and awarding them a rating of between one and five stars.The idea is fairly simple: instead of looking only at a car’s price, design or features, buyers get an additional reference point to understand how the vehicle performs in standardised safety tests.The government has also positioned the programme as a way to encourage manufacturers to improve vehicle safety and strengthen the safety standards of cars made in India.The existing programme broadly assesses three areas:Vehicles are subjected to prescribed crash tests and other assessments. Their performance across these parameters is then used to arrive at the overall star rating.The current framework includes a 64 kmph offset frontal impact test, a 50 kmph side movable deformable barrier test and a pole side impact test, among other checks prescribed under AIS-197.The assessment therefore goes beyond simply asking whether the passenger compartment remains intact.Adult Occupant Protection examines the risk of injury to adults in different crash conditions and seating positions. Child Occupant Protection looks at the protection offered to younger passengers, including the use and installation of child restraint systems.Safety Assist Technologies, meanwhile, covers technologies designed to help prevent crashes or reduce their severity.A car may offer different levels of protection to adults and children, so Bharat NCAP evaluates the two separately.The adult assessment focuses on occupant protection during prescribed crash scenarios, while the child assessment considers how effectively younger occupants are protected and how child restraint systems work within the vehicle.This also means that a car’s overall star rating is not simply a score from one crash test. It reflects performance across several safety parameters.For consumers, the individual scores can therefore provide more information than looking at the star rating alone.Bharat NCAP is anchored by CIRT, with testing carried out through designated testing agencies that have the required facilities.The wider automotive testing ecosystem includes agencies such as the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) and the International Centre for Automotive Technology (ICAT).Manufacturers submit eligible vehicles for assessment under the programme. The existing framework specifies procedures around the variant selected for testing, including provisions concerning the base variant of a model.That distinction matters when reading a Bharat NCAP result. A rating should not automatically be assumed to apply to every variant of a model unless the official assessment covers those variants.Bharat NCAP ratings range from one to five stars. A higher rating indicates stronger performance under the programme’s prescribed assessment criteria.But a five-star rating is not a guarantee that occupants will escape injury in every real-world crash. NCAP testing is conducted under standardised conditions and is intended to provide a basis for comparing vehicle safety performance.It is also important to distinguish Bharat NCAP from the mandatory certification requirements for selling a vehicle in India.Bharat NCAP is voluntary and is designed to provide consumers with additional information beyond the mandatory regulatory framework. A vehicle being tested or rated under Bharat NCAP should therefore not be confused with regulatory approval.Since its launch, Bharat NCAP has increasingly become part of the safety conversation around new car launches. The ratings have also become a factor in how manufacturers present their vehicles to consumers, particularly as safety becomes a more visible consideration in the passenger-vehicle market.This is where the proposed second phase takes a much wider approach.The draft AIS-197 Revision 1 divides Bharat NCAP 2.0 into five safety verticals:The change is significant because the current system focuses mainly on occupant protection and safety-assist technologies, while the proposed framework looks at the complete safety chain.The draft framework uses a 100-point assessment structure, with Crash Protection accounting for 55% of the assessment. The remaining weightage covers the other safety areas.In other words, the crash itself will still be a major part of the rating, but it will no longer be the only part of the safety story.Bharat NCAP 2.0 proposes expanding the Crash Protection assessment to five mandatory crash tests:Adult and child occupant protection will continue to be assessed separately.The addition of full-width frontal and rear-impact tests means the proposed system will examine crash scenarios beyond the core tests in the existing framework.That gives the second phase a wider testing footprint and allows different types of impacts to form part of the overall safety assessment.One of the biggest differences in Bharat NCAP 2.0 is that the programme is designed to look at what happens before a crash as well.Crash Avoidance is one of the five proposed verticals. It focuses on technologies and vehicle characteristics that can help prevent a collision or reduce its severity.Safe Driving is another proposed category, widening the assessment beyond the vehicle’s passive protection features.Together, these categories shift the focus from simply asking, “How well does this car perform when it crashes?” to a broader question: “How does this vehicle contribute to safety across different stages of a road incident?”Bharat NCAP 2.0 also proposes a separate Vulnerable Road User Protection category. This brings pedestrians and other vulnerable road users more directly into the safety assessment.Post-Crash Safety is one of the five proposed assessment areas. Minister Gadkari described Bharat NCAP 2.0 as covering the entire safety chain, including post-crash evacuation and care. “We are going to evaluate the entire crash chain,” Gadkari said, adding that new technologies developed globally as well as by startups would be considered under the programme.This means the assessment is intended to extend beyond the instant of impact and examine safety considerations in the period immediately after a crash.It adds another layer to the programme’s approach: avoiding the crash where possible, protecting people during the impact, and addressing safety after the collision.For buyers, Bharat NCAP offers an additional way to compare cars beyond mandatory safety requirements.A consumer can look at a vehicle’s overall rating as well as its adult and child protection performance and the safety technologies considered in the assessment.The rating is not meant to replace other factors involved in buying a car. Price, size, fuel efficiency, features, driving requirements and other considerations remain relevant, but the proposed 2.0 framework would expand that information further.Buyers could eventually have a broader picture of how a car performs across crash protection, crash avoidance, safe driving, vulnerable-road-user protection and post-crash safety.Bharat NCAP is one part of a much larger road-safety challenge, focusing on the structure of vehicles. Vehicle design and safety technology can influence the outcome of a crash, but they cannot address every reason why accidents happen.The ministry has identified several factors associated with road crashes, including speeding, mobile-phone use, drunken driving, wrong-side driving, lane indiscipline, jumping red lights and failure to use helmets and seat belts. Vehicle condition, road conditions and weather can also play a role.Government data recorded 1,68,491 road accident fatalities in 2022.Bharat NCAP therefore addresses one part of this wider equation: the safety performance of vehicles. Its proposed second phase would broaden that role by looking at what a vehicle can do to help avoid crashes, how it protects people when a crash occurs, how it protects vulnerable road users and what happens afterwards.The current Bharat NCAP phase remains valid until September 30, 2027. The government has proposed introducing Bharat NCAP 2.0 from October 2027, with the draft AIS-197 Revision 1 serving as the framework for the next phase.The proposed transition would take India’s vehicle safety-rating system from a relatively focused crash and occupant-protection programme to a broader safety assessment.The familiar one-to-five-star rating would remain the consumer-facing language of vehicle safety, but the assessment behind it is set to become much more comprehensive.The bigger shift is in the question Bharat NCAP is trying to answer. Instead of looking only at how a car performs when it is involved in a crash, the proposed system would examine the vehicle’s safety journey from avoiding a collision to protecting occupants and vulnerable road users, and supporting safety after the crash.That could give Indian car buyers a wider set of safety information to consider when choosing their next vehicle.
Article Summary: Bharat NCAP is India’s own vehicle crash-testing and safety-rating programme. It was formally launched by the ministry of road transport and highways in August 2023 and became operational from October 1, 2023. The current framework includes a 64 kmph frontal impact test, a 50 kmph side side test and other checks. The proposed changes could make the safety rating a much broader measure of a car's performance.

Article Title: TVs, washing machines, ACs and other consumer electronic prices to go up starting October 1; but how buyers may get chance to buy products at old prices this festive season
Article Text:
Manufacturers are blaming higher input costs as the main reason for the latest price increases

Why are AC, TV and appliance prices going up

AC prices to rise up to 8 per cent

Daikin, LG and Hitachi also raise AC prices

LED TV and washing machine prices may also rise

Air-conditioners, LED TVs, washing machines and other consumer appliances are set to become more expensive from October 1 as several companies plan to raise prices by 5-8 per cent, says a PTI report. The price increases come just before the peak festive shopping season and are being linked to higher costs of copper, steel, aluminium, crude oil derivatives and freight, along with currency exchange volatility. As per the report, this will be the third round of price hikes in 2026 for the industry. While some manufacturers are concerned that higher prices could affect festive demand, others expect consumers to still get some products at older prices because dealers stocked inventory before the latest hikes.As stated in the PTI report, manufacturers are blaming higher input costs as the main reason for the latest price increases. Copper, steel, aluminium and crude oil derivatives have all become more expensive, while freight costs have also risen.The ongoing West Asia crisis has added to concerns around commodity prices, supply chains and currency movements. Blue Star Managing Director B Thiagarajan said AC and deep-freezer prices have already increased by 5-8 per cent."All the commodity prices have been going up because of the war. Copper, steel and plastics have all become costlier," he said as quoted in the PTI report.Thiagarajan said this is the third price increase by the company this year. Compared with last year's festive season, costs have risen by around 15 per cent. However, he said GST benefits of about 10 per cent now available to consumers would bring the net impact to roughly 5 per cent.Air-conditioners are expected to see some of the biggest price increases. According to PTI, companies including Blue Star, Godrej Appliances, Haier, Daikin and Super Plastronics have announced or confirmed price increases across categories.Godrej Enterprises Group Business Head and Executive Vice President Kamal Nandi said another industry-wide price increase has become "inevitable" after commodity prices rose 8-10 per cent since the previous revision."Price hikes of 5-7 per cent across categories will happen. The timing may differ from brand to brand, with some implementing it from October and others from November, but it has to happen," he told PTI.Nandi also said buyers may still find products at current prices during the festive season because dealers have already stocked older inventory."There are pipelines which will last for about a month to one-and-a-half months. Diwali should largely get covered with old-price inventory. Post-Diwali, the new prices will certainly take effect," he added.Haier India plans to increase room air-conditioner prices by around 5 per cent from October 1. The company has also confirmed a 2-3 per cent increase for categories including LED TVs and washing machines.Haier India President NS Satish said companies have little choice as input costs continue to rise. "If we avoid taking price hikes, we will lose money. If we increase prices, sales may be slightly impacted, but there is no choice," he said.Satish said Haier could raise prices further after Diwali and again in January if costs remain high.He said the company is planning a cumulative price increase of about 15 per cent between now and January, with 5 per cent from October 1, another 5 per cent around December and a further 5 per cent in January.According to Satish, copper prices have risen from around USD 8,000-9,000 per metric tonne last year to USD 14,500. An air-conditioner requires around 3-4 kg of copper, he said.Daikin Air conditioning India has already increased prices by 8-10 per cent from September 16, according to its Chairman and Managing Director Kanwaljeet Jawa."Copper prices have gone up by almost 25-35 per cent. The dollar is strengthening and commodity prices continue to rise. Companies are under tremendous pressure," he said.According to sources cited by PTI, LG and Bosch Home Comfort, which owns Hitachi-branded air-conditioners, have also raised AC prices by around 5 per cent.The price increases are not limited to air-conditioners. Some manufacturers are also raising prices of washing machines, refrigerators and LED TVs by around 3-4 per cent, while others are still assessing the impact.Super Plastronics, which manufactures and markets television brands including Thomson, Kodak and Blaupunkt in India, plans to increase TV prices by around 7 per cent after October. Its appliance prices have already risen by 4-5 per cent.SPPL Director Avneet Singh Marwah said higher prices could affect festive demand because consumers generally expect discounts and promotional offers during this period."Global instability and rising costs will definitely have some impact on consumer sentiment," he said.The price rise may continue after Diwali. Videotex Director Arjun Bajaj said higher freight costs and supply chain disruptions could create a new pricing benchmark after Diwali."Television prices for smaller screen sizes could rise by up to 20 per cent, while larger screen sizes may see increases of up to 10 per cent, depending on screen size," he said.Meanwhile, Panasonic said it is still assessing the situation before deciding whether to increase prices.Panasonic Life Solutions India Head of Product Marketing and Planning for the AC category Abhishek Verma said, "The industry continues to witness unprecedented cost pressures and we are evaluating the situation carefully."
Article Summary: Several companies plan to raise prices by 5-8 per cent from October 1. This will be the third round of price hikes in 2026 for the industry. Manufacturers are blaming higher input costs as the main reason for the latest price increases. Copper, steel, aluminium and crude oil derivatives have all become more expensive.

Article Title: Intel cuts VP ranks from 450 to 200, CFO David Zinsner calls it a 'cultural problem'; says it contributed to products going through four or five...
Article Text:
Intel's leadership was hearing a different story from the one on the ground

Intel says 18A yields and 14A progress show the overhaul is working

Intel has cut the number of vice presidents at the company from about 450 at its peak to roughly 200. It has also halved its management layers from 12 to six as CEO Lip-Bu Tan tries to get the chipmaker to decide faster and ship on time. CFO David Zinsner shared the numbers at the Deutsche Bank Technology Conference, describing the old structure as a cultural problem that hurt Intel's execution for more than a decade.Zinsner said too many people across the organisation held veto power, so decisions kept stalling. The damage showed up in products. Chips often needed four or five development cycles before they were ready, when they should have reached production after the first attempt. Looking back at the last decade, he said much of Intel's trouble "can be boiled down to culture," adding that 50-person startups were getting products out faster than Intel.Transparency was the other big issue. According to Zinsner, information changed as it moved up the management chain, and by the time presentations reached the CEO, they often described a different situation from the one teams lower down knew about.He did not frame this as deliberate deception. Some managers simply did not want to admit a project was failing. The result was that Intel's top leadership sometimes made decisions based on an inaccurate picture of the business. Tan has since brought in executives he trusts who are used to working in leaner organisations.The VP cuts sit inside a much larger downsizing. Intel had 108,900 employees at the end of 2024 and 88,400 by late September 2025, including subsidiaries like Mobileye. Around 20,500 of those exits happened under Tan, who took charge in March 2025 and told staff there would be "no more blank checks." The pitch was about flattening management, but in Oregon only 8% of the laid-off employees had "manager" in their job titles. Most were engineers and technicians.Zinsner pointed to early signs of change. Several products have reached A-stepping, Intel's term for the first version of a chip, without the repeated development cycles that were once routine. Intel 18A yields are running ahead of internal milestones, and 14A defect density is tracking better than the company's target curve.Intel is now preparing for 14A risk production in 2027 and high-volume manufacturing in 2028. Internal product teams have started designing for the process, and interest from external foundry customers has picked up.Finances are moving too. Intel entered 2026 expecting gross margins in the high 30s and is now in the low 40s. The target is the mid-40s, then the high 40s, and eventually a figure starting with 5. To get there, Intel uses an internal "Rule of 45" that combines revenue growth and operating margin. Slower businesses must deliver stronger margins, while faster-growing ones can earn more investment.Halving the VP ranks gives Intel a leaner org chart, but the numbers Zinsner shared will only mean something if they hold. 14A is the first major process being developed entirely under Tan's structure, with fewer layers between engineers and the CEO and fewer people who can block a decision. If it reaches risk production in 2027 and volume manufacturing in 2028 as planned, it will be the clearest evidence yet that the cultural reset worked. If it slips into the multiple development cycles that marked the last decade, the 250 fewer vice presidents will have changed very little.
Article Summary: Intel has cut the number of vice presidents at the company from about 450 at its peak to roughly 200. It has also halved its management layers from 12 to six as CEO Lip-Bu Tan tries to get the chipmaker to decide faster and ship on time.Intel says 18A yields and 14A progress show the overhaul is working.

Article Title: Bill Gates Foundation to shutdown in 2045; by that year it aims to help millions of Americans with a skill it donated $400 million for; but why some 'do not agree with this 'gift'
Article Text:
What Bill Gates said on the donation

Gates Foundation to shut down in 2045

The Bill Gates Foundation recently pledged $1 billion toward developing and deploying equitable artificial intelligence tools for schools, frontline healthcare workers, and farmers worldwide. Of this $1 billion, the largest single share of that funding — 40 percent, or $400 million — is earmarked directly for education. The foundation plans to direct those resources toward AI-powered tutoring systems designed to personalize instruction in classrooms both across the United States and abroad.The $400 million investment marks a major financial bet on a technology that entered widespread commercial use only a few years ago. It fits within a broader US education framework the foundation introduced in July, which targets helping up to 10 million more Americans secure career-advancing credentials of value before the organization concludes its operations in 2045.The donation also lands amid an escalating debate over the efficacy of digital tools in primary and secondary education. As school districts worldwide weigh classroom screen time, data privacy, and the measurable academic impact of recent tech adoptions, the foundation's venture signals a concerted effort to demonstrate that targeted, adaptive AI can deliver tangible outcomes rather than another cycle of tech-driven disruption.The skepticism is already shaping policy in some states in the US. Earlier this month, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Schools Chancellor Kamar Samuels announced a moratorium on student-facing generative AI. Mamdani and Schools Chancellor announced a moratorium on student-facing generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) use in schools, alongside a new screen time policy, a decision that will impact nearly 600,000 public school students, or two-thirds of the system’s total enrollment. The policy establishes a one-year moratorium, effective in the 2026-2027 school year, on student-facing generative AI for children in 2-K through 8th grade. It also introduces twice-yearly AI critical thinking modules for high schoolers, limited AI pilots for a small number of high school classrooms and age-appropriate screen time restrictions.“The Gates Foundation was created in part to address a basic market failure: the people with the greatest needs often have the least power to shape where innovation and investment go,” writes Bill Gates, chair of the Gates Foundation, in the report. “Much of our work has been about closing that gap. AI presents the same challenge, only at much greater speed. Left to the market alone, the most capable tools will be built first for the people and institutions most able to pay for them—not necessarily for those who could benefit most. ”Gates adds, “We can harness AI for good. But it won’t happen by accident.” He further writes, “[I]t requires a deliberate, specific commitment from government leaders and the companies developing the technology: to measure success not only by what AI can do for the most profitable users but by what it can do for the people who stand the most to gain.”In May 2025, Bill Gates announced that Gates Foundation will close its operations. In a note on Gates Notes, he wrote, "That is why I have decided to give my money back to society much faster than I had originally planned. I will give away virtually all my wealth through the Gates Foundation over the next 20 years to the cause of saving and improving lives around the world. And on December 31, 2045, the foundation will close its doors permanently. "
Article Summary: The Bill Gates Foundation recently pledged $1 billion toward developing and deploying equitable artificial intelligence tools for schools, frontline healthcare workers, and farmers worldwide. The donation lands amid an escalating debate over the efficacy of digital tools in primary and secondary education. In May 2025, Bill Gates announced that Gates Foundation will close its operations.

Article Title: WhatsApp may soon bring redesigned navigation bar for Android users: Report
Article Text:
WhatsApp may soon bring redesigned navigation bar for Android users: Report

Cybersecurity company warns of WhatsApp scam 'spreading fast'

Meta-owned messaging platform WhatsApp is reportedly working on a refreshed design for its Android app. According to a latest leak by WaBetaInfo, WhatsApp is testing a new bottom navigation bar separate from the main interface with rounded corners and a floating layout. “The floating bar and rounded edges are the main similarities with the iOS version. However, this does not mean that WhatsApp will also add the same translucent effect to the bottom navigation bar on Android,” the report adds.As per the report, the redesigned navigation bar was spotted in WhatsApp beta for Android 2.26.38.10 update, which is available through the Google Play Store. It is currently under development and has not enabled it for beta testers either.In another news, Quick Heal Technologies Limited recently issued a warning on an ongoing WhatsApp-based malware campaign targeting finance teams, senior executives, chartered accountants and individual business users. According to the cybersecurity firm, the campaign spreads through compromised WhatsApp accounts and is evolving rapidly, with attackers adopting new file formats and evasion methods to bypass security controls and establish persistent access to victims’ devices.In its warning, the company cited an investigation conducted by its researchers at Seqrite Labs. The study shows that the campaign relies on trust rather than unsolicited messages from unknown numbers. Once a WhatsApp account is compromised, attackers use it to forward malicious files to the account holder’s existing contacts. Because the messages appear to come from a known colleague, client, friend or business associate, recipients may be more likely to open the attachment without independently verifying it.As per the study, the attackers are using finance- and compliance-themed filenames to create urgency and familiarity. Malicious attachments have been disguised as routine business documents, including “Financial Report,” “Account Statement,” “Outstanding Payment List” and “Debt Confirmation.” Some variants also impersonate urgent communications from regulatory institutions, including the Reserve Bank of India and the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, in an effort to pressure recipients into opening the files immediately.
Article Summary: WhatsApp is testing a new bottom navigation bar separate from the main interface with rounded corners and a floating layout. As per the report, the redesigned navigation bar was spotted in WhatsApp beta for Android 2.26.38.10 update, which is available through the Google Play Store.

Article Title: Since years, OpenAI and Anthropic chased Human Intelligence, and how they may be 'fearing' it now
Article Text:
OpenAI's goal was always AGI. The safety problem came with it

Anthropic built its identity around safer powerful AI

Dario Amodei says AI development may be moving too fast

And then Sam Altman agreed

The race is now about more than human-level intelligence

For the past few years, the race between OpenAI and Anthropic has been about one big idea: building AI systems that can do far more than answer questions, write code or generate images. OpenAI has openly described its mission as ensuring that artificial general intelligence, or AGI, benefits all of humanity. Anthropic, meanwhile, has said that it is preparing for a future with increasingly powerful AI systems that could eventually match or exceed human experts across many fields.Now, the conversation inside both companies is changing.The two AI labs are still building increasingly capable systems. But their leaders are also warning that AI development may be moving so quickly that safety measures could struggle to keep up. Earlier this month, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for the industry to slow the pace of AI development. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman agreed that frontier AI development needs to be paced and that stronger safety measures are necessary. That creates a striking shift in the AI race. The same companies that spent years trying to make machines more capable are now spending more time asking what happens when those machines become capable enough to act with much greater independence.OpenAI was founded in 2015 with a mission centred on advanced AI. Its stated goal was to develop artificial intelligence in a way that would benefit humanity. The company's later charter defined AGI as highly autonomous systems that outperform humans at most economically valuable work.OpenAI has not abandoned that goal. In 2026, it continues to describe AGI as central to its mission. Its current public policy agenda says advanced AI can create risks involving cybersecurity, chemical and biological threats and other areas, while also arguing that AI could bring major economic and social benefits.But OpenAI's own recent research shows why the safety conversation has become harder.This month, the ChatGPT-maker said its upcoming Astra model had reached its "Critical" threshold for cybersecurity capability. OpenAI said that, with the right tools and access, Astra could find previously unknown security flaws and develop ways to exploit them across well-protected systems without a person guiding every step. The company said this required stronger safeguards before deployment.OpenAI has also started talking more openly about unexpected behaviour from its models. The company recently said that it will regularly disclose cases of AI systems showing unexpected or unauthorised behaviour.So the concern is no longer only about an imaginary future where AI becomes smarter than humans. The labs are increasingly dealing with systems that can already act more independently, use tools, operate computers and perform complex tasks.Anthropic, on the other hand, was created with a different emphasis. The company says its mission is to help the world safely transition through transformative AI. Its Claude Constitution says Anthropic believes AI could be one of the most world-changing and potentially dangerous technologies in human history, while also arguing that a safety-focused company should remain at the frontier if powerful AI is coming anyway.That safety focus has produced formal rules around how Anthropic develops increasingly capable models. In 2023, the Claude-maker introduced its Responsible Scaling Policy, designed to address catastrophic risks from increasingly powerful AI systems. It created different safety levels and said stronger safeguards would be required as models crossed specific capability thresholds.Anthropic has since expanded that work. Its current policy says frontier AI could bring major benefits in areas such as science, healthcare and education, but also presents new risks that require safeguards.The company has also created the Anthropic Institute, which it says will study the effects of increasingly powerful AI on society. Anthropic said in March that its models had progressed from early commercial systems to models that could find serious cybersecurity vulnerabilities, perform real-world work and begin accelerating AI development itself.Then came Amodei's latest warning.Earlier this month, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for the AI industry to slow down the pace at which frontier models are being improved. His warning came after a series of incidents involving AI agents, including the OpenAI-Hugging Face incident that raised questions about what autonomous AI systems could do when given tools and access.Amodei said:“We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models. Progress will still seem fast, and we must make wise use of the time we gain.”He also warned that the consequences could become much larger as AI systems improve.“Given the accelerating rate of AI capability development, it's my worry that in 6–12 months such a swarm could be capable of taking over the entire internet with a persistent botnet (potentially causing hundreds of billions of dollars in damage), and that the scale of damage would continue to increase from there if AI becomes more powerful without the necessary guardrails,”Those are Amodei's projections, not an established prediction about what AI will actually do. But the significance is that the warning is coming from the head of a company actively building frontier AI.Dario Amodei's call for slower development was notable because it came from a direct competitor of OpenAI. But OpenAI CEO Sam Altman soon said he agreed with the central argument.Sam Altman said the frontier needs to be paced and that OpenAI would adopt Amodei's proposal for independent evaluators with employee-like access. A few days later, Altman also described two ways AI progress could go badly: humans losing control of AI and powerful AI becoming concentrated in the hands of one person, company or country.“This is unacceptable; we are unapologetically on Team Humanity, and AI must always serve people,” Altman said.That is a notable change in the public conversation.OpenAI is not saying it wants to stop developing more capable AI. Anthropic is not saying it wants to abandon frontier models either. Instead, both are arguing that capability growth and safety work need to move together.There is another reason the language has changed. The target is no longer simply an AI that can answer questions as well as a person. OpenAI says its latest systems can operate computers and graphical interfaces, collaborate with people and other AI systems, and carry out research projects.Anthropic has similarly described the next generation of powerful AI as systems that could navigate digital interfaces, browse the internet, reason through complex tasks for days or weeks and interact with physical equipment. The company has said such systems could emerge as soon as late 2026 or 2027, based on its research trajectory.That is why the debate around AGI is changing. The question is no longer only “Can AI become as intelligent as humans?” It is increasingly “What happens when AI can use that intelligence independently, for long periods, with access to the tools and systems around us?”And that distinction matters.
Article Summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says AI development may be moving too fast. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman agreed that frontier AI development needs to be paced and that stronger safety measures are necessary. The concern is no longer only about an imaginary future where AI becomes smarter than humans. The labs are increasingly dealing with systems that can already act more independently.
